articles.title: Russell Brand called a ‘ruthless’ sexual predator as rape and sexual assault trial begins in London; 51-year-old comedian pleads not guilty to three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault
articles.summary: Russell Brand was described as a “ruthless” and manipulative sexual predator by a prosecutor as his rape and sexual assault trial began at Southwark Crown
articles.body: Russell Brand was described as a “ruthless” and manipulative sexual predator by a prosecutor as his rape and sexual assault trial began at Southwark Crown Court in London on Wednesday. According to The Associated Press, the 51-year-old actor-comedian has pleaded not guilty to three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault involving six women. The alleged offences took place between 1999 and 2009.Opening the prosecution's case, prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones told jurors that the six women, who did not know one another, were allegedly assaulted at different locations, including a hotel room, workplaces, a bar's toilet cubicle and Brand's home.She alleged that Brand had an “indiscriminate and voracious” desire for sexual contact at the time, adding that “women were simply a means to an end”.The prosecutor acknowledged that Brand could be funny and charming but described him as “a flirt with a huge sexual appetite — childlike in his expectation that his every desire should be met”.“He was ruthless, he was calculating, he was manipulative. And, the prosecution say, he was a sexual predator,” Karmy-Jones told the jury.Six women have made allegations spanning a decadeThe court heard details of the allegations, which span a decade. The earliest complainant alleges that Brand raped her in a hotel room in 1999, during the Labour Party's annual conference in Bournemouth, where he was performing at a fringe cabaret event.Another woman alleges that, in 2001, Brand tried to drag her into a men's bathroom at the office building where she worked.“There can be little doubt as to what Mr Brand's intention was,” Karmy-Jones said.A third woman alleges that Brand orally raped her in a London bar's restroom in 2004. According to the prosecution, when she asked him to stop, he told her, “Don't be a spoilsport.”The remaining allegations include an incident at a London radio station in 2004 or 2005, when a woman alleges that Brand kissed and groped her, leaving her feeling “dirty and disgusting”.Another complainant, who was 21 at the time, alleges that Brand anally raped her at his home in 2009 after she met him at one of his shows.The prosecutor told the court that the woman exchanged text messages with Brand the following year, telling him, “You treated me like an animal.” He allegedly replied, “I'm sorry.”The sixth complainant alleges that Brand demanded a massage and pressed his face into her groin while an advertisement was being recorded in 2009.Prosecutor explains why the women did not report the alleged assaults earlierKarmy-Jones told jurors that none of the women reported the alleged incidents to the police at the time. She said they were held back by feelings of guilt and shame, as well as concerns that they would be blamed.According to the prosecution, the women independently approached the police after a television programme broadcast anonymous allegations against Brand in 2023.The prosecutor said the jury would hear directly from the complainants during the trial, adding, “I have no doubt you will find their evidence compelling.”Former friend recounts 1999 trip to BournemouthThe first witness to testify was Mark Pinheiro, a former friend of Brand who accompanied him on the trip to Bournemouth in 1999.Pinheiro told the court that Brand made them leave the town abruptly the day after the alleged rape and appeared “incredibly alert and incredibly afraid”.“Whenever a police siren passed the car, Russell would cower down behind the side window so he couldn't be seen,” he said.Brand's lawyer, Ian Winter, questioned Pinheiro's recollection of events that allegedly took place more than 25 years ago.Brand has denied all the charges. During police interviews, he denied ever engaging in non-consensual sexual activity.Russell Brand says he feels ‘blessed’ ahead of trialBrand arrived at court on Wednesday amid a crowd of photographers and video journalists. Speaking briefly, he said he felt “blessed” and expressed hope that the legal proceedings would lead to a positive outcome.“I feel, of course, concerned but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved,” he said. “That's my prayer.”Known for his risque stand-up comedy and highly publicised struggles with drugs and alcohol, Brand rose to prominence in the early 2000s. He hosted television programmes and a BBC radio show before appearing in Hollywood films such as ‘Forgetting Sarah Marshall’ and ‘Get Him to the Greek’. He was also briefly married to pop star Katy Perry.In recent years, Brand has moved away from mainstream media, relocated to Florida and built a substantial online following through videos discussing wellness, conspiracy theories and his religious beliefs.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘New Girl’ star Jake Johnson lists $3.295 million Pasadena home with a pool, sauna-equipped sunroom and two detached structures
articles.summary: Actor Jake Johnson, best known for playing Nick Miller on New Girl and co-hosting the comedy podcast We’re Here to Help, has listed a Pasadena,
articles.body: Actor Jake Johnson, best known for playing Nick Miller on New Girl and co-hosting the comedy podcast We’re Here to Help, has listed a Pasadena, California, home for $3.295 million. The contemporary-style residence has 3,153 square feet of living space, 4 bedrooms and 4 bathrooms, and sits behind private gates on a lot of nearly half an acre, according to published reports. Its features include a swimming pool, landscaped grounds, 2 detached structures and a sunroom with a sauna. Thomas Atamian of Coldwell Banker Realty is handling the listing. The home was built in 1947 and remodelled in 2004 by architect Aleks Istanbullu, according to the listing details reported by the media. Whether the home sells at its $3.295 million asking price remains to be seen, but its gated privacy, pool, sauna-equipped sunroom and flexible detached studios give it broad appeal for buyers seeking a creative, wellness-oriented Pasadena retreat.Jake Johnson’s Pasadena home listing: what $3.295 million buysThe home combines a contemporary interior with extensive outdoor space. Reports describing the listing mention hardwood floors, wood accents, large windows and open living and dining areas that look out towards the grounds. The property sits behind private gates, with mature landscaping helping to screen it from the street. The grounds include a swimming pool, outdoor areas for relaxing and dining, and a garden featuring California native plants and fruit trees, according to published descriptions. Listing agent Thomas Atamian has emphasised the property’s privacy and the flexibility offered by its additional structures.The asking price is $3.295 million, although some media reports round it to $3.3 million or $3.29 million. These are rounded versions of the same asking price, rather than evidence of separate listings. The property’s appeal rests on its combination of indoor living space, outdoor grounds and additional buildings.Sunroom sauna and spa-inspired bathroom: inside the primary suiteThe primary suite includes a vaulted ceiling, a fireplace and a walk-in closet. The adjoining bathroom features Italian blue glass mosaic tile around a soaking tub and a separate shower, according to descriptions of the listing. A sunroom equipped with a sauna is another feature of the property. The sunroom and sauna are part of the home’s wellness-focused amenities, but descriptions of the layout should be read carefully because reports do not always distinguish clearly between the sunroom and the detached wellness structure. The listing photographs, credited to Hillary Campbell and supplied by Coldwell Banker, show the primary suite, bathroom, sunroom and other interior spaces.The house has also served as a place for Johnson’s creative work. The Pasadena Star-News reported that the walk-in closet had previously been used as a creative space for his comedy podcast, We’re Here to Help. The detail offers a glimpse of how the property has been used beyond its role as a residence.Two detached structures and a creative pastThe 2 detached structures add flexible space beyond the main house. According to the listing description quoted in media reports, they can accommodate uses such as working from home, creative projects and wellness activities. Their layout and previous uses are more specific than the general description of two additional studios might suggest. In a 2023 interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Johnson described using one of the structures as a creative escape for his projects and another as a wellness space with an adjoining sunroom. That account provides context for the buildings’ previous uses, although it should not be taken as confirmation of their permitted uses or current configuration.The listing identifies the property as a contemporary architectural residence remodelled by Aleks Istanbullu in 2004. Public-record reporting has also raised a distinction between the listing’s association with Johnson and the name on the property title. The property has been reported as held by the Poppy Lou Trust, which acquired it for $2.215 million in April 2017. That purchase price is a historical figure, not the current asking price, and the trust’s ownership should not be presented as proof that Johnson personally holds title. The current listing brings together a gated setting, landscaped grounds, a pool, a sauna-equipped sunroom and two detached structures. Its asking price is $3.295 million, but the property’s eventual sale price, if sold, may differ from that figure.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Twitter Users Are Losing It After Melania Trump's Advisor Says Her Movie Performed Better Than Tom Cruise's: 'This Is Hilarious'
articles.summary: Social media users are slamming Melania & her advisor after he boasted that her documentary was doing better than 'Digger.' Read more at SheFinds.com.
articles.body:
Twitter users are mocking Melania Trump 's senior advisor after he tried to boast about the first lady's documentary outperforming Tom Cruise's latest movie, Digger , at the box office.

The advisor, Marc Beckman, took to social media to highlight the films' opening-weekend earnings per theater, arguing that Melania had the stronger performance despite opening in fewer theaters. However, his attempt to celebrate the documentary's numbers has prompted plenty of ridicule online, with critics pointing out that both films struggled commercially and that the first lady's project received overwhelmingly negative reviews. Read more about his post and how the internet reacted below.

Melania Trump's Advisor Boasts About Her Documentary Outperforming Tom Cruise's 'Digger' On X

Tom Cruise's latest film, Digger , recently hit theaters, but the political satire had a disappointing opening weekend despite the Hollywood star's leading role. According to entertainment outlets, the film earned approximately $8 million domestically and $20 million worldwide, making it a significant box-office disappointment for a production reportedly costing between $160 million and $180 million.

Rather than letting the film's disappointing numbers speak for themselves, Melania Trump's senior advisor Marc Beckman seized the opportunity to promote the first lady's documentary, Melania , which was released in January. He claimed that the documentary outperformed Digger by approximately 67% on a per-theater basis, despite playing in roughly half as many theaters.

However, while Melania earned around $7.16 million during its opening weekend, it went on to gross approximately $16.7 million worldwide amid widespread criticism and poor reviews.

Twitter Users Mock Melania's Advisor Over His Box Office Comparison

The advisor's attempt to see the comparison as a win for the first lady 's documentary quickly attracted criticism, with social media users questioning why he was celebrating a movie's performance by comparing it to another film that had also struggled at the box office.

Many also pointed to the documentary's reported production and marketing costs, arguing that earning more per theater than Digger was hardly the impressive achievement he suggested. Others simply found the comparison hilarious, using the opportunity to poke fun at both the advisor's post and the highly criticized documentary.

"So it outperformed one of the biggest bombs ever?" responded an X user. "Quite an achievement, being slightly less of a bomb."

"Yeah, but Digger is an interesting film actually about something, and Melania is a godawful piece about a vain, vapid model, history's worst First Lady , who exists staring at herself in the mirror, trying on clothes and yammering about her 'creative vision,'" slammed another.

"This is hilarious," one user wrote, as another responded, "Man, that's some lame number crunching you're doing there. Anyone who has ever read a spreadsheet is laughing at you."

"That's like saying this sewer rat is prettier than this other sewer rat," a user joked. "Please sit down."

"Just give up already," added another. "No one respects her."

articles.title: 'Sense and Sensibility' star Esmé Creed-Miles grew up with famous parents. She's candid about what that gave her.
articles.summary: Esmé Creed-Miles talks "Sense and Sensibility," growing up with actor parents and her bond with Daisy Edgar-Jones.
articles.body:
Esmé Creed-Miles knows a thing or two about yearning. Onscreen, it involves windswept hair, beautiful dresses and a Jane Austen romance. At home, it's a 1 a.m. grocery order with her girlfriend. Their current obsession: frozen chocolate-covered raspberries.

"They're probably full of rubbish, but we feel like they're healthy because they have fruit in them," she tells Yahoo, laughing.

It's a persuasive argument and a glimpse of the 26-year-old behind Marianne Dashwood, the passionate heroine she plays opposite her close friend Daisy Edgar-Jones in Sense and Sensibility, in theaters on Friday . Creed-Miles identifies with Marianne's intensity of feeling. Her enthusiasm for a crowded ballroom? Less so.

"I'm a lot more shy than Marianne," she says. "It was fun to kind of transform a little bit in that way."

Already familiar to viewers as the young assassin at the center of Hanna , Creed-Miles grew up the daughter of English actors Samantha Morton and Charlie Creed-Miles, with an early sense that a film set was somewhere she belonged. She's candid about the privilege that came with that upbringing, including the confidence to speak up in places that can feel inaccessible to others.

"I don't walk into these spaces feeling like, 'Oh, I don't belong here,'" she says. "I actually feel like I really belong on a film set."

Still, knowing your way around a set doesn't make the industry any less unpredictable. For that, it helps to have Edgar-Jones, who plays Marianne's sister, Elinor, and whose bond with Creed-Miles extends well beyond the Dashwood household.

"We really have each other's backs, and we care deeply for one another," Creed-Miles says. "It is a really tough industry to navigate, so to have a best friend to do it with is everything."

For Yahoo's Generation Now series, Creed-Miles discusses stepping into Austen's world, the parts of the 1800s she's happy to leave behind and why, when it comes to appreciating her mom's talent — most recently on display in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey — everyone else is simply catching up.

Marianne isn't afraid to make a fool of herself for something she believes in. How was it playing someone who puts herself out there so completely?

I think there's something really special about someone loving outside of the bounds of what's expected of them, especially for the time. So I think she's kind of a maverick in that sense.

She's not impressionable in the way [of the] standards of etiquette and conformity. She kind of exists beyond them and in rebellion of them. And I think that's really, really special about her. I love that.

How much of yourself did you see in Marianne?

I saw a lot of myself in regard to the intensity of feeling that she experiences. But I would say I'm a lot more shy than Marianne.

At the ball, she is just so full of life. She really gets in there and sinks her teeth into the social aspect of that. It was very community-focused back then, and I think she really enjoyed that. And I'm not like that. So it was fun to transform a little bit in that way.

Between the costumes, the windswept hair and all the yearning, what part of being a Jane Austen heroine did you most enjoy? And what were you happy to leave in the 1800s?

Lots I was happy to leave in the 1800s! But the context of these women's lives really shaped them as people, and I think it gave a really amazing texture for us to explore the characters. When there are those kinds of tribulations stacked against a person, it brings out really interesting qualities in them.

The place that we find these women in at the beginning of the movie, they're essentially kicked out of their homes. … So obviously that's one element that's, like, very much, thank you, that's in the past.

Beyond that, I think it was just fun to exist in another world. There was a lot of craft that went into the costume and the general mise-en-scène. It's very intentional and lived-in. We wanted everything to feel like these were actual pieces of clothing that they wore. So it was really nice to build a world and have it be authentically inhabited by us for that period of time.

Looking at this story through a modern lens, Marianne feels like someone people might describe as "too much." Did playing her make you think about how quickly we ask young women to tone themselves down?

I don't know. I think the way that we inhabit gender and the power that plays between gender is obviously something that hasn't been completely reconciled anywhere in the world, I don't think.

So to be exploring that dynamic in the context of 200 years ago and have it feel relevant for today is special. And if it makes people think about that and the things that we as women want to protect, then that's important.

You've described Daisy as family. In an industry that can feel pretty unpredictable, what does it mean to have someone you trust alongside you during a moment like this?

It's really everything. It was very important to Georgia [Oakley, the film's director] and to all of us making this film that we were trying to centralize the female love story, the sisterly love story between Elinor and Marianne.

At the end of the movie, you get a sense that regardless of what has happened with them in their love lives, whether they got the guy or they didn't get the guy, they have each other. I hope the audience walks away with that feeling.

Me and Daisy definitely inhabit that in our own lives as well. We really have each other's backs, and we care deeply for one another. It is a really tough industry to navigate, so to have a best friend to do it with is everything. Couldn't do it without her, for sure.

With both your parents being actors, what did you understand about this line of work growing up that someone on the outside might not?

People talk a lot now about privilege when it comes to growing up with certain access, and I think it's an important conversation. It's not one that I necessarily feel shy of. It doesn't bother me.

But I also think that the main privilege that comes from growing up or existing in that space is that you have a certain sense of belonging. The arts can feel, and rightly so, so inaccessible because they are, to an extent, inaccessible.

I think in the U.K., something like 90-plus percent of the creative workforce come from financially stable homes. So we're really depriving our cultural output of diverse voices, and I think that's a real shame.

But the privilege I have from growing up with people who are in the industry is that I have a sense of belonging in these spaces. I feel like I understand them. I feel like I have a voice in those spaces. I feel like I'm able to form opinions from a place of experience. And I've also seen representation for people who look like me and sound like me.

So I don't walk into these spaces feeling like, "Oh, I don't belong here." I actually feel like I really belong on a film set. And I know how they work, every in and out of how a film set works. I think it'd be amazing if more people were able to experience that from an early age or were given an understanding of that.

Your mom is having such a celebrated moment with 'The Odyssey.' What's it been like watching people discover — or rediscover — someone whose talent you've known your whole life?

She really deserves it, so I'm so proud. And it's amazing to see, although I will say, maybe it's just a U.K. thing: She's always been this larger-than-life presence in the industry and where I grew up.

So for me, I'm like, "Duh." For me, she is this formidable presence. So it just feels like everyone's catching up!

You make music as well as act. When you're not working, what does life as a normal 26-year-old look like for you?

I have a band with my best friend, Evie. She's a string player, and we make music and we play it. That would be my other life, I suppose. But I think the two things complement each other.

There are so many different ways to express an inner life, and I'm just very lucky that I get to make art. That's really the greatest joy.

This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

articles.title: ‘Only Modi can tour’: Mann slams Paris denial after Japan
articles.summary: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann slams Centre/MEA for denying clearance to visit SIAL Paris food festival; cites repeated rejections, calls it political bias.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Thursday criticised the Centre for denying him political clearance to visit Paris, where he has been invited to attend a food festival featuring a Markfed exhibition stall.Replying to a question, Mann told media in New Delhi, “What do we do? There is a food festival being held in Paris, and we received an invitation from the French govt, with Markfed putting up a stall. Earlier, I was also scheduled to travel to Japan for three days to watch the semi-finals and finals of the hockey matches. Since we are hosting the Men’s Hockey Asian Champions Trophy starting Oct 27, we also wanted to extend a formal invitation to them in person.”Hitting out at the Narendra Modi-led Centre, Mann added, “They simply refuse to give me permission (to travel abroad). It seems as though only PM Modi can tour the world—visiting even the most obscure places like Papua Guinea, ‘Manglesia,’ or ‘Changlesia.’ We have now moved the high court, and I hope to receive approval tomorrow. Our goal in traveling is strictly to benefit Punjab, attracting investors so we can create employment opportunities for our youth.”The food festival in question refers to SIAL Paris, touted as the world’s largest and most influential food innovation exhibition and trade fair held biennially at Paris Nord Villepinte exhibition centre.This is not an isolated incident, as CM Mann and his members have repeatedly been denied political clearance by the ministry of external affairs (MEA) for foreign visits. In Aug 2024, the Centre blocked Mann’s proposed trip to Paris to attend the Olympics and cheer on the Indian men’s hockey team, citing diplomatic and administrative reasons.Prior to this, Mann and then-industries minister Sanjeev Arora were denied approval for a planned investment outreach tour to the UK and Israel ahead of Progressive Punjab Investors’ Summit. More recently, MEA refused him clearance to travel to Japan for the Asian Games hockey semi-finals on security grounds.In Sept 2022, Punjab minister Aman Arora was refused approval for an official knowledge-sharing tour to Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands. Also, assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan was denied clearance to attend a legislative speakers’ conference in the US in Aug 2024. Minister Harbhajan Singh was blocked from representing Punjab’s governance model at a conference in Boston in Aug last year.Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leadership has termed these rejections politically motivated, alleging partisan political discrimination by the Centre toward Punjab.In contrast, neighbouring Haryana’s chief minister Nayab Singh Saini has consistently been granted prompt political clearances for his international delegations and investment tours. Recently, Saini led a high-level state delegation on a three-day official visit to Singapore from Oct 4 to Oct 6 to pitch investment, urban infrastructure, and trade partnerships. articles.summary: Tem também muitas opções gratuitas para curtir a cidade: como a 8ª Parada LGBTQIA+ do Itaim Paulista, e o Festival Cartografias de Bamba na Barra Funda.
articles.body:
Pitty se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Stephanie Rodrigues/g1

A cidade de São Paulo tem um fim de semana de programação intensa, com a 50ª Mostra Internacional de Cinema, que reúne 380 filmes de 93 países até 29 de outubro, e a Viradinha 2026, festival infantil gratuito com mais de 400 atividades espalhadas por todas as regiões da capital. Para quem prefere música ao vivo, a agenda inclui Pitty, Barão Vermelho, Rashid, Jorge Vercillo e Dionne Warwick, que apresenta sua turnê de despedida na cidade.

O fim de semana também tem opções gratuitas para curtir a cidade: a 8ª Parada LGBTQIA+ do Itaim Paulista reúne shows e atividades culturais na Zona Leste, enquanto o Festival Cartografias de Bamba ocupa a Rua do Samba da Barra Funda com apresentações musicais, batalha de rima, literatura e gastronomia. No Parque Ceret, no Tatuapé, o 1º Festival de Comida Árabe da Zona Leste reúne mais de 40 expositores, além de atrações culturais e atividades para toda a família.

No teatro, a programação vai de clássicos infantis, como “João e o Pé de Feijão”, a montagens que misturam música e literatura, como o encontro entre o maestro João Carlos Martins e o escritor Gabriel Chalita. Há ainda concertos gratuitos da OCAM-ECA/USP com a obra de Mahler e apresentações para crianças, como “Planeta Peteca”, de Cris Barulins. Para quem gosta de cinema ao ar livre, o Centro Cultural São Paulo recebe uma sessão de “It: A Coisa” com música ao vivo, enquanto o BikeCine exibe filmes com energia gerada pelas pedaladas do público.

50ª Mostra Internacional de Cinema de São Paulo

Coletiva de imprensa da 50ª Mostra Internacional de Cinema em São Paulo — Foto: Mario Miranda Filho/Agência Foto

A 50ª Mostra Internacional de Cinema de São Paulo reúne 380 filmes de 93 países até 29 de outubro, em sessões espalhadas por 57 salas de cinema, espaços culturais e CEUs da capital. A programação começa nesta quinta-feira (15) e inclui mais de 100 produções brasileiras, além da terceira edição da Mostrinha, voltada ao público infantil.

Um dos destaques desta edição comemorativa é o cineasta norte-americano James Gray, responsável pela arte do cartaz do festival. Ele participa da abertura para apresentar Tigre de Papel (Paper Tiger), seu novo filme, que também terá sessões comerciais durante a Mostra. A programação reúne produções de diferentes países e gêneros, com opções para públicos variados.

📍 Onde? Em 57 salas de cinema, espaços culturais e CEUs de São Paulo

💲 Quanto? De segunda a quinta-feira: R$ 26 (inteira) e R$ 13 (meia-entrada). De sexta a domingo: R$ 32 (inteira) e R$ 16 (meia-entrada)

”Vaqueiro Benedito e a Cobra Caninana” junta teatro com forró na Biblioteca Mário de Andrade — Foto: Divulgação

Palhaços, acrobatas, malabaristas e contação de histórias estão entre as atrações da Viradinha 2026, festival infantil gratuito que acontece de sexta-feira (16) a domingo (18), em todas as regiões de São Paulo. Em sua segunda edição, o evento reúne mais de 400 atividades para crianças, com espetáculos, oficinas criativas e shows musicais.

A programação circense inclui atrações como “PixuShow”, do Circo Bem Bolado, “As Charlatonas”, da Trupe Açu, e apresentações do Circo do Asfalto, que celebra 20 anos de trajetória. Há também espetáculos para bebês e crianças pequenas, como “Broto de Circo”, da Trupe Germinar. As atividades acontecem em espaços culturais da cidade, com horários variados.

📅 Quando? De sexta-feira (16) a domingo (18), em horários variados

📍 Onde? Em espaços culturais de todas as regiões de São Paulo

6ª Parada do Orgulho LGBTQIA+ de Itaim Paulista — Foto: Reprodução/Paulo Neobeck

articles.body:
Festival Mada começa nesta sexta-feira (16) na Arena das Dunas, em Natal — Foto: Bia Azvedo/Mada

O Festival Música Alimento da Alma (Mada) 2026 começa nesta sexta-feira (16) e segue até sábado (17), na Arena das Dunas, em Natal. A programação reúne artistas como Zeca Pagodinho, Marina Sena, Duquesa, Emicida, Gaby Amarantos e BaianaSystem, além de atrações do Baile da Amada.

Os portões serão abertos às 18h30 nos dois dias. Para ajudar o público a se organizar, o g1 reuniu os horários dos shows, a lista de itens permitidos e proibidos, informações sobre ingressos e orientações para chegar ao local.

A programação é dividida entre três espaços: Palco MADA, Palco Petrobras e Palco TIM, que recebe o Baile da Amada. As apresentações começam antes das 20h e seguem até a manhã do dia seguinte.

21h às 22h30 — Zeca Pagodinho, com participação de Karinah

0h às 1h10 — Tribo de Jah convida Célia Sampaio

19h50 às 20h50 — Delusis convida Sad Bruno

Os horários foram divulgados pela organização do festival. Como há apresentações simultâneas em palcos diferentes, vale conferir a programação antes de chegar e planejar quais shows assistir.

A organização divulgou regras para a entrada de objetos na Arena das Dunas. Entre os itens permitidos estão:

Até dois alimentos industrializados para consumo próprio, como barras de cereal e biscoitos;

Câmeras analógicas, como Instax e Polaroid.

A lista de itens permitidos deve ser conferida com atenção antes de sair de casa. Em caso de dúvida sobre algum objeto, o recomendado é consultar os canais oficiais do festival.

Caixas de som e dispositivos que produzam som alto.

A relação também inclui objetos e substâncias ilícitas. A entrada está sujeita à fiscalização de segurança.

O festival será realizado na Arena das Dunas, na Avenida Prudente de Morais, nº 5.121, no bairro Lagoa Nova, em Natal.

Quem for de carro pode consultar previamente as opções de estacionamento e os acessos disponíveis. A Arena das Dunas informa que o estacionamento interno tem entrada pela Avenida Lima e Silva, enquanto o estacionamento externo tem acesso pela Rua Projetada, ao lado do Centro Administrativo. A disponibilidade pode variar em dias de evento.

Também é possível chegar de transporte público. Como as linhas e condições de circulação podem mudar, a recomendação é verificar os itinerários atualizados antes de sair.

Sobre os portões de entrada : a abertura ao público está prevista para as 18h30 nos dois dias. O portão específico de acesso deve ser confirmado no ingresso ou nos canais oficiais do festival, conforme o setor adquirido.

Quem não puder comparecer à Arena das Dunas também poderá acompanhar parte da programação pela TV Globo e Inter TV. A transmissão está prevista para depois do Jornal da Globo, nesta sexta-feira, e depois do Altas Horas, no sábado, além de exibição pelo Globoplay, conforme a programação divulgada.

A cobertura será exibida para os nove estados do Nordeste, os cinco estados da região Norte, além de Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais. Será a primeira vez que a transmissão do Mada chegará aos estados da região Norte.

articles.title: Spice Girls: clipe de 'Wannabe' faz 30 anos e esconde corte | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo foi gravado em hotel abandonado em Londres depois que a locação original, em Barcelona, teve a autorização negada. VÍDEO mostra curiosidades do 1º clipe gravado pela girl band.
articles.summary: O clipe de 'Wannabe' das Spice Girls completa 30 anos revelando um corte escondido e bastidores curiosos em um hotel abandonado de Londres.
articles.body:
Há 30 anos, as Spice Girls lançavam o primeiro clipe do quinteto, “Wannabe”. O vídeo é lembrado como um plano-sequência, filmado sem cortes. Na prática, há uma emenda, que seria aos 2 minutos e 46 segundos de vídeo, embora não confirmada pela equipe que criou o vídeo.

A ideia era gravar em um prédio em Barcelona, com as cantoras invadindo uma festa. Cinco dias antes das filmagens, a autorização foi negada. A produção levou o clipe ao St. Pancras Renaissance Hotel (antigo Midland Grand Hotel), que estava abandonado no centro de Londres. Por lá, fazia muito frio e havia pouca iluminação.

O resultado parece espontâneo, mas boa parte do que surge na tela foi coreografada. O grupo repetiu o trajeto várias vezes antes de começar a gravar, e a equipe fez de 10 a 15 gravações completas .

Na edição, o diretor uniu a primeira metade impecável de um take à segunda metade de outro. A emenda parece estar escondida no momento em que a câmera mostra uma TV exibindo o clipe.

Alguns takes foram descartados, incluindo os que Geri Halliwell tropeçou e caiu porque estava de salto alto.

As Spice Girls no clipe de 'Wannabe', de 1996 — Foto: Reprodução

A direção é do sueco Johan Camitz, que nunca tinha feito um clipe. Quatro anos depois, ele morreu em um acidente ao ser atropelado por um motorista que havia sido baleado.

Antes do sucesso, o vídeo enfrentou resistência. Executivos da gravadora Virgin consideraram a música e o clipe estranhos e anárquicos demais. A preocupação aumentou porque rádios como a BBC 1 se recusaram a tocar a música assim que ela foi lançada.

Os executivos também acharam as roupas das cantoras justas e transparentes demais. Chegaram a querer que o clipe fosse regravado, mas desistiram da ideia.

Meses depois, “Wannabe” passou a ser exibido na TV inglesa e entrou na programação da MTV. A música ficou um mês no topo da Hot 100 da "Billboard" e se tornou o primeiro hit das Spice Girls.

Geri, Mel C, Victoria, Mel B e Emma: as Spice Girls — Foto: Divulgação/Virgin Records

articles.title: Pitty reprocessa chip do punk rock em álbum que também acena para a pista do pop contemporâneo e para o metal | G1
articles.standfirst: Também editado em LP, o disco oferece grandes momentos, como a balada 'Caminhada', mas deixa o gosto amargo de que a artista andou para trás.
articles.summary: Também editado em LP, o disco oferece grandes momentos, como a balada 'Caminhada', mas deixa o gosto amargo de que a artista andou para trás.
articles.body:
Pitty lança o sexto álbum solo de estúdio nesta sexta-feira, 16 de outubro, com 12 músicas — Foto: Jorge Daux / Divulgação

♬ Aperitivo do sexto álbum solo de estúdio de Pitty, o single “Sobremesa” deixou gosto meio agridoce no ar. Era um rock voraz de cepa punk que, embora saboroso, sinalizava retrocesso na discografia de artista que há sete anos lançara “Matriz” (2019), grande álbum em que Pitty trocou o chip e expandiu a sonoridade, passando a Bahia natal pelo filtro do rock.

No mundo a partir de hoje, sexta-feira, 16 de outubro, em edição digital e em LP fabricado pela gravadora Deck, o álbum intitulado “Pitty” tem o mesmo sabor de “Sobremesa” em parte das 13 faixas, formatadas com produção musical orquestrada por Rafael Ramos com a própria Pitty.

É como se “Matriz” não tivesse existido na trajetória fonográfica da cantora, compositora e instrumentista baiana.

Em essência, ao longo do álbum “Pitty”, a artista reativa o chip do punk rock em músicas como a assertiva “Não à deriva”, faixa que tangencia o stoner rock, e flerta com o peso do metal em “Desobediente”, faixa que termina com toques da música oriental na produção feita com a adesão de Nave.

Até aí tudo bem. O álbum traz de volta a Pitty de outrora, mas com a experiência dos 49 anos – completados em 7 de outubro – e com a maturidade de quem já atravessou problemas de saúde, pariu uma filha já pré-adolescente e amargou uma separação cujas dores são expiadas nos versos do blues-rock “Álbum de casamento”.

“Eu vou botar no papel tudo o que doer / É caminho pra absorver, trilha pra elaborar / ... / Devolva minhas senhas, eu confiei em você / A minha autoestima, não precisa devolver / Eu já tomei de volta a posse do que é meu / Minha arte, meu corpo, minha maternidade / A minha insanidade quem resolve sou eu”, determina Pitty, dando o tom altivo das letras do álbum, cujo repertório é inteiramente assinado pela artista, sem parceiros.

Pitty faz acerto póstumo de contas com a mãe nos versos do rock-balada 'Cuidada' — Foto: Jorge Daux / Pitty

O corpo estranho no álbum “Pitty” é “Pileque de poeta”, faixa feita com a adesão de Felipe Vassão (coprodução, programação e teclados) que acena para a pista do pop contemporâneo, fora de sintonia com o tom do álbum. “Sobriedade seletiva”, outra faixa formatada com a colaboração de Vassão, soa mais integrada à atmosfera roqueira do álbum por harmonizar elementos de punk-disco e house.

Com letra endereçada à destinatária de identidade desconhecida, “Amiga,” também se diferencia no conjunto da obra, soando como um rock em flerte fugaz com o universo do tecnobrega.

Curiosamente, o álbum se agiganta quando os beats se desaceleram e a guitarra de Martin Mendonça perde a fúria que sustenta músicas como “Armadura”.

Esse crescimento é nítido em “Caminhada”, balada em que Pitty versa sobre sororidade feminina. “Não estamos sozinhas, embora tentem dizer / Que a nossa única escolha é ceder ou morrer / A gente se reconhece pelo rastro e pela voz / O que tentaram quebrar em ti dói em todas nós / Não aceito que te calem, não aceito o teu fim / Cuidar de você é também cuidar de mim”, ressalta Pitty.

Já o rock-balada “Cuidada” é afetivo acerto póstumo de contas de Pitty com a mãe, Laurita, já falecida. Em outra letra interessante, Pitty se dirige à mãe com a experiência de ela, Pitty, já ser mãe de Madalena.

No geral pautado pela fúria incandescente das guitarras, sobressalentes em faixas como “Madame” e harmonizadas com o baixo de Paulo Kishimoto, a bateria de Nico e os teclados de Rodrigo Tavares, o álbum “Pitty” termina com “Nó”, rock sobre recomeço.

“Pior que cair é nem tentar andar”, sentencia a roqueira em verso de “Nó”. Por mais que o álbum “Pitty” deixe a sensação de que a artista deu dois passos para trás, o fato é que Pitty tem se mantido de pé, em movimento.

Capa do álbum 'Pitty' — Foto: Jorge Daux / Divulgação

articles.title: 'Hanuman Ansh' box office collection day 70: Vishal Chaturvedi film earns Rs 65 lakhs; worldwide gross reaches Rs 448.33 cr; India net collection stands at Rs 338.98 cr
articles.summary: Vishal Chaturvedi's 'Hanuman Ansh' collected Rs 65 lakhs in India net earnings on its 70th day in theaters.
articles.body: Vishal Chaturvedi's 'Hanuman Ansh' collected Rs 65 lakhs in India net earnings on its 70th day in theaters. According to Sacnilk, the film recorded 1,672 shows across its Hindi and Telugu versions on Thursday, October 15. Its cumulative India net collection has reached Rs 338.98 cr, while the domestic gross stands at Rs 400.03 cr.The movie collected Rs 10 lakhs in overseas gross revenue on Day 70, taking its cumulative overseas gross to Rs 48.30 cr. Its worldwide gross collection has now reached Rs 448.33 cr. However, Thursday's domestic net earnings declined by 48% compared with the Rs 1.25 cr collected on Wednesday. The film recorded an overall occupancy of 13.2% across its reported shows.'Hanuman Ansh' Day 70 box office collectionThe Hindi version contributed Rs 35 lakhs from 1,262 shows, registering 11% occupancy. Meanwhile, the Telugu version earned Rs 30 lakhs from 410 shows, with occupancy reaching 20%. Together, the two versions generated Rs 65 lakhs in India net collections on Thursday.The Hindi 2D version recorded 12.02% overall occupancy. Morning shows registered 7.50%, followed by 12.50% in the afternoon and 14.50% in the evening. Night shows recorded 13.58%. The Telugu 2D version registered 14.89% overall occupancy, with morning shows at 13%, afternoon shows at 11.78%, evening shows at 13.78% and night shows at 16.33%.'Hanuman Ansh' day-wise box office collectionThe film began its 10th Friday with Rs 1.20 cr before collections increased over the weekend. Saturday brought Rs 2.50 cr, while Sunday recorded Rs 2.80 cr. Earnings subsequently declined during the weekdays, with Rs 1.25 cr on Monday, Rs 1.35 cr on Tuesday and Rs 1.25 cr on Wednesday. Thursday's Rs 0.65 cr collection marked another drop.'Hanuman Ansh' week-wise box office collectionThe film's highest reported weekly collection came in Week 5, when it earned Rs 90.25 cr. articles.body: Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' has opened strongly at the box office, raising hopes for another hit for the superstar. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, the film sees Rajinikanth return as Muthuvel Pandian, also known as Tiger. The action scenes, star cast, and mass moments have caught the attention of fans. As per Hindustan Times, the deal was locked for Rs 160 crore, and the film is expected to premiere on the platform on November 12, 2026. The deal includes a four-week theatrical window, meaning the Rajinikanth-starrer is expected to arrive online around a month after its cinema release. The anticipated OTT premiere will give fans, who missed the film on the big screen, an opportunity to watch it at their comfort. However, the streaming date has yet to receive official confirmation from Amazon Prime Video or the makers, and November 12 should therefore be considered a tentative date.'Jailer 2' cast and crewThe sequel to the 2023 blockbuster 'Jailer' features a star-studded ensemble led by Rajinikanth. The cast includes Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Mithun Chakraborty, Mohanlal, and Shivarajkumar, among others. Nelson Dilipkumar returns as director, while Sun Pictures backs the ambitious project. Anirudh Ravichander has composed the music, adding to the anticipation surrounding the film’s soundtrack and action-packed sequences. The movie’s star-studded cast, with actors from different industries has helped it reach beyond the shores of Tamil Nadu and make a good start.Will 'Jailer 2' be able to continue its streak?'Jailer 2' has been receiving good reviews and feedback from viewers. articles.title: Vicente Vallés cuestiona el uso de la Diputación Permanente por parte del Gobierno para intentar aprobar los decretos de vivienda: “Trampeo político”
articles.standfirst: El presentador de 'Antena 3 Noticias 2' cerró la semana en ‘El Hormiguero’
articles.summary: El presentador de 'Antena 3 Noticias 2' cerró la semana en ‘El Hormiguero’
articles.body: Este jueves, 15 de octubre, ‘El Hormiguero’, programa que presenta y dirige Pablo Motos en el ‘access prime time’ de Antena 3, cerró una nueva semana con la visita de Vicente Vallés, reconocido periodista de nuestro país y presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias 2’. El presentador acudió al espacio de Atresmedia para presentar ‘Espías: clave secreta’, su serie documental de historia y espionaje disponible en Onda Cero. Así le presentó Motos: “Él viene de aquí al lado, le tenemos controlado por el GPS y ya ha llegado. Es invitado platino, una ovación para él”. Vallés entró en un BMW por todo lo alto al plató entre aplausos y vítores del público, agradeciendo el televisivo la calurosa bienvenida. El presentador de ‘El Hormiguero’ se interesó por la obra del invitado, que había sido escrita, narrada y dirigida por él. “A los espías les hubiera gustado ser periodistas y a los espías, periodistas. Ambos tienen similitudes, nos queremos enterar de cosas que nadie conoce. Un espía cuando conoce algo se lo comunica a personas importantes para que tomen decisiones y los periodistas salimos a contarlos corriendo”, contestó Vicente Vallés. “No sería un buen espía, por eso me dedico al periodista”, añadió Vallés entre risas. Posteriormente, charlaron de varios entresijos de la citada obra del comunicador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias 2’. “Me fascinan los espías ilegales, que los forman, los mandan a un país, tienen pareja, hijos y los activan. Es un argumento espectacular en una película”, apostilló Motos, visiblemente impresionado tras escuchar la trama de ‘Espías: clave secreta’. En este sentido, el comunicador de Requena quedó impresionado al comprobar de primera mano que los espías de la obra de Vallés mantienen la “intriga” en todo momento: “Su vida siempre está en juego, puede pasar cualquier cosa en cualquier momento. Pueden ser detenidos a las cinco de la mañana porque los han descubierto o alguien de su departamento se pasa al enemigo y los delata”, añadió el presentador de noticias al respecto. “Desde que empecé a escribir e informarme de estos temas, decidí desconectar, porque si no, no lo haces. Pensarías todo el rato”, afirmó Vicente Vallés acerca de la intriga que le causó componer su obra por todas las preguntas que plantea. Tras ello, llegó el momento de hablar de los mejores servicios secretos del mundo, saliendo a escena el CNI y su gestión en la crisis de Ceuta: “Es muy negativo tirar piedras contra el tejado de tus propios servicios de inteligencia. Visto con la perspectiva de los dos meses y pico que han pasado, da la sensación de que la imagen del CNI ha salido reforzada y la del Gobierno, perjudicada. Ha sido un intento del Gobierno de salvarse a sí mismo”, recalcó Vallés. Con lo que respecta a las consecuencias judiciales por lo sucedido en Ceuta dijo que irá por “mucho tiempo”, pero que es “firme” cuando actúa. Asimismo, Vicente Vallés dijo que la ciudadanía merecía saber que una fragata marroquí había estado en aguas ceutíes justo cuando se produjo el asalto y no “ocultarlo”. Otro de los temas es el adelanto electoral por parte de Pedro Sánchez, presidente del Gobierno, al 29N, algo que llevó a Motos a cuestionarle sobre si habrá debate electoral en Antena 3, a lo que contestó el invitado. “Esperemos que sí. Dependemos de los partidos políticos”. Llegando al tramo final de la entrevista, Motos le preguntó sobre los dos decretos de la vivienda y el uso de la Diputación Permanente por parte del Ejecutivo actual para intentar aprobarlos de cara a paliar la crisis, algo de lo que se pronunció de manera tajante: “Hay quien dice que es legal, pero es un trampeo político. Un decreto rechazado por el pleno no debería ser aprobado por un organismo cuyos miembros no representan la misma composición de diputados que el pleno del Congreso. Cuando te dicen que no, es que no. Habría que esperar a las elecciones”. El problema cree que se solucionará en un “periodo largo de tiempo”, pero que no sabe cuál es la solución. Ante este tipo de adversidades pidió unidad a todas las formaciones políticas de España: “En los grandes asuntos de Estado, los partidos tienen que entenderse”. Por último, ante las acusaciones de fraude electoral ante el voto por correo de cara al 29N por parte de Ayuso, Feijóo y Abascal, Vallés lo tiene claro: “Hay que tener algunas pruebas para demostrarlo y no basarse solo en sospechas. Hay mucha gente que considera que ya se ha producido un fraude que todavía no ha ocurrido”.

articles.title: ‘One of the biggest challenges of riding is people’s perception’: Fatima Sana Shaikh
articles.summary: For Fatima Sana Shaikh, biking is more than a thrill, it is a meditative experience that offers a sense of freedom and perspective.
articles.body: For Fatima Sana Shaikh, biking is more than a thrill, it is a meditative experience that offers a sense of freedom and perspective. The actress, whose film Dhak Dhak took her through the challenging terrains of Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh, recently bought a new bike that she got customised. The actress says riding has taught her as much about endurance as it has about the joy of the open road.In an exclusive interview with us, she also calls out the gender stereotypes and harassment women riders continue to face, arguing that riding a motorcycle should not be seen as extraordinary simply because the rider is a woman.What sparked your love for biking, and what does being on a bike give you that you don’t experience in any other aspect of your life? Is it the sense of freedom, the thrill of the open road or the feeling of being completely in the moment?I don’t remember the exact moment I fell in love with biking. But as a child, my father would take me along for a short ride on his bike every evening. So, for me, bikes have always been associated with happiness and excitement. In fact, my father was also the first person who taught me how to ride. Riding is such a beautiful feeling. It’s very liberating. I don’t know how to explain it exactly, but there’s something incredible about being able to control a machine that almost becomes an extension of your body. Even the slightest shift in your body weight can change the direction of the bike. I find that fascinating. And especially when you’re riding in the mountains, it’s such a humbling experience. You realise how small and insignificant you are in the larger scheme of things. You feel the temperature dropping, the wind, the changing landscape. You’re experiencing everything around you rather than just watching it go by. I find riding very meditative.What has been the most memorable or rewarding part of your biking journey so far? Is there a particular ride, destination or experience that made you fall in love with biking all over again?I think it was when I was shooting for Dhak Dhak. I got to ride in Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh, and honestly, I don’t think I would have ever dared to ride in the mountains otherwise. But shooting for that film and riding through those terrains made me realise that biking isn’t just about the fun and excitement. It’s tough. Especially when you’re riding long distances or touring. It’s physically and emotionally demanding, and I got a taste of that during the shoot. But it also made me realise how rewarding the experience can be. And ever since then, I’ve wanted to do a proper bike trip on my own. Hopefully, I’ll get to do that soon.Biking comes with its share of challenges, especially for women riders. What have been some of the biggest hurdles you’ve faced on the road, and how have these experiences shaped you as a rider?One of the biggest challenges is people’s perception. We’re so used to associating bikes with men, so when a woman rides one, it suddenly becomes this extraordinary thing. And honestly, that’s kind of ridiculous, because at the end of the day, it’s just a vehicle. You learn, you practice, you get better. Just like anything else. But what really troubles me is that sometimes it doesn’t stop at perception. We’ve seen instances of women riders being pushed, intimidated, harassed on the road. It’s almost as if the audacity of a woman riding is so upsetting to some people that they’d rather harass her than just let her be. And that is really sad. I think we need to stop attaching gender to something as basic as riding a vehicle. I don’t ride to prove a point. I ride because I enjoy it. I just hope we get to a point where seeing a woman on a motorcycle is just as normal as seeing a man.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Hope' actor Jung Ho-yeon calls ‘3 Idiots’ an inspiration; praises the joy in Hindi films: 'They are really about joyfulness'
articles.summary: South Korean actor Jung Ho-yeon has spoken about her appreciation for Indian cinema, naming Aamir Khan’s ‘3 Idiots’ as a film that continues to resonate
articles.body: South Korean actor Jung Ho-yeon has spoken about her appreciation for Indian cinema, naming Aamir Khan’s ‘3 Idiots’ as a film that continues to resonate with her. The actor believes Hindi films have a distinctive ability to celebrate happiness and bring joy to audiences. She also hopes to create something that leaves viewers with a similar sense of positivity.In a conversation with Variety India, Jung Ho-yeon discussed the qualities she admires in Hindi cinema. She recalled watching ‘3 Idiots’ and explained why its approach to storytelling appealed to her. The actor also shared her desire to work on a project that makes people happy.Jung Ho-yeon recalls watching ‘3 Idiots’Jung Ho-yeon praised the emotional quality she associates with Indian films, particularly their emphasis on happiness. She said she wants to explore stories that can offer audiences the same kind of joy. “I watched ‘3 Idiots’, and I always love that about Hindi films. They are really about happiness. They are really about joyfulness. I truly want to do something that makes people happy and brings joy,” Ho-yeon said.Why Aamir Khan’s ‘3 Idiots’ remains memorableReleased in 2009, ‘3 Idiots’ was directed by Rajkumar Hirani and starred Aamir Khan, R Madhavan, Sharman Joshi and Kareena Kapoor Khan. The film follows three friends whose experiences challenge conventional ideas about education, success and personal fulfillment. Through comedy and friendship, the story examines the pressure students face to meet academic expectations. It also questions an education system that often places achievement above individual interests and creativity.Jung Ho-yeon looks forward to ‘Hope’The actor is also anticipating the Indian theatrical release of ‘Hope’, a science fiction thriller written, directed and co-produced by South Korean filmmaker Na Hong-jin. The project brings together performers from South Korea and Hollywood. The ensemble cast includes Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Taylor Russell, Cameron Britton, Alicia Vikander and Michael Fassbender.What is ‘Hope’ about?‘Hope’ follows a village police chief and his rookie deputy as they try to protect their community from a mysterious creature. Their efforts unfold as a hunting party in the surrounding mountains encounters a threat of its own. The film blends science fiction with monster-movie elements, placing a small community at the center of an extraordinary situation. Its story moves between familiar rural surroundings and an increasingly dangerous mystery. The movie is getting good reviews from the critics.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Karthik Subbaraj and 'Dorothy' team meet Minister Vanni Arasu over transphobia, seeks strict action and dedicated helpline for transgender community
articles.summary: Director Karthik Subbaraj’s latest film 'Dorothy' has drawn attention for its portrayal of transgender lives and social issues.
articles.body: Director Karthik Subbaraj’s latest film 'Dorothy' has drawn attention for its portrayal of transgender lives and social issues. The film, which stars Keerthy Suresh, Rishikanth and Sananth, was released on September 25. Karthik Subbaraj also produced the project, while Ilaiyaraaja composed the music for the film.Minister Vanni Arasu promises action on transgender community’s concernsThe 'Dorothy' team recently met Tamil Nadu Social Justice Minister Vanni Arasu at the state government secretariat. The minister praised the film for starting an important conversation about social change and challenging caste-based discrimination. During the meeting, Karthik Subbaraj also requested stricter rules and action against transphobia, along with a dedicated helpline for the transgender community. According to the director, the minister agreed to take up these requests. Vanni Arasu also spoke about the need for more films that question social barriers and promote equality.Karthik Subbaraj shares details of 'Dorothy' team’s meetingSharing pictures from the meeting on X, Karthik Subbaraj thanked the minister for recognising the film’s message. He wrote, “Honourable Minister Mr.Vanni Arasu sir felicitated team #Dorothy at Tamilnadu Government Secretariat and appreciated our film as an important Cinema that has started a healthy conversation and change in the Society.” He added, “He also took my request to implement strict rules and actions to curb Transphobia in any form and also to have a dedicated Helpline for the transgender community.” The director concluded his post with the words, “Thanks a lot sir. Your words of praise and endorsement to our film means a lot to us..”Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu calls for more films that challenge social discriminationSpeaking to reporters after the meeting, Vanni Arasu praised the filmmakers for addressing deep-rooted social issues. “It is encouraging to see directors come forward to break caste structures,” he said, as reported by Nakkheeran, adding that 'Dorothy' had opened up a new conversation about the transgender community. He also expressed hope that more films would explore such subjects.'Dorothy' has received appreciation from several members of the film industry, including directors Mani Ratnam and Shankar. Superstar Rajinikanth had also met the team and praised their work. With the latest meeting bringing attention to the director’s request, the discussion around 'Dorothy' has moved beyond cinema to the need for stronger protection and support for transgender people.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: What happened in Juventus Women's last victory against Como 1907?
articles.summary: The Women's First Team are back in Serie A Women action after the international break, which saw Italy beat Belarus 3-1 on aggregate over two legs in a World...
articles.body:
The Women's First Team are back in Serie A Women action after the international break, which saw Italy beat Belarus 3-1 on aggregate over two legs in a World Cup qualifier.

The Bianconere's Matchday 3 game sees them host Como 1907 in Biella. This is actually the very first match in Serie A between the two teams, with Como being promoted from Serie B during the summer.

The teams have met once before already this season, though, so let's take a look at what went down.

You don't have to cast your minds back very far to remember what happened when Juventus last beat Como 1907. It came just two months ago, when Juventus travelled to Lombardy for a Serie A Women's Cup group match.

There has been much excitement around Como 1907 and the squad they have put together for their first Serie A campaign, but Juventus asserted their dominance with a 2-0 victory.

Whilst it was a closely contested match, Alba Redondo gave the Bianconere the lead in the 25th minute. She reacted quickest to a loose ball in the box to open the scoring.

There was a feeling that the match could have gone either way, but in the 79th minute, Remina Chiba showed great awareness to head in when a cross bounced back off the post.

That victory set Isaac Guerrero's team on a journey that would eventually lead them to retain the Serie A Women's Cup title, remaining the only team that has managed to win the tournament.

articles.title: ‘Godfather’ star Al Pacino to receive life achievement award from actors’ guild
articles.summary: Celebrated actor Al Pacino will receive a lifetime achievement award for his career achievements and humanitarian work next year, the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA said.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — Celebrated actor Al Pacino will receive a lifetime achievement award for his career achievements and humanitarian work next year, the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA announced on ​Thursday. The American actor, best known for playing Michael Corleone in “The Godfather” films, is ‌the 62nd recipient of the SAG-AFTRA Life Achievement Award. The union will present the award to him in Los Angeles at the 33rd Actor Awards on February 28, 2027 as part of a ceremony to be ​live-streamed on Netflix. Pacino’s recognition follows a career spanning more than six decades across film, ​television and stage. He is known for numerous memorable characters, including real-life police ⁠officer Frank Serpico in 1973’s “Serpico,” Miami mobster Tony Montana in 1983’s “Scarface” and more recently Hollywood ​agent Marvin Schwarz in Quentin Tarantino’s 2019 film “Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood.” The award is presented ​annually to an actor who embodies the “finest ideals of the acting profession,” according to the union. “I wondered and wandered most of my life but have always felt at home with a script and my fellow actors,” ​Pacino said in a statement from the actors’ union. “It’s the work and the actors along the ​way that have been among the greatest joys of my life. It’s an honor to be recognized by ‌SAG-AFTRA ⁠in celebrating the journey,” he added. Pacino won the Best Actor Oscar for his performance as Lieutenant Colonel Frank Slade in the 1992 film “Scent of a Woman,” and has also won multiple Emmy, Tony and Golden Globe awards. “Like so many actors, I have spent my life in awe and ​appreciation of the force ​of nature that ⁠is Al Pacino. When you watch him perform, you are witnessing a student and a master,” SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin added in the statement. Pacino ​also participated in the “America: A Tribute to Heroes” telethon following the September ​11, 2001 ⁠attacks, and in 2009 received the Arthritis Foundation’s Jane Wyman Humanitarian Award for his charitable work. The 86-year-old actor was born Alfredo James Pacino in New York. He struggled throughout the 1960s to find ⁠steady work ​before his eventual film breakthrough in 1972’s “The Godfather.” SAG-AFTRA represents ​approximately 160,000 actors, broadcast journalists, dancers, DJs, news writers, program hosts, puppeteers, recording artists, singers, stunt performers, ​voiceover artists, influencers and other entertainment and media professionals.

articles.title: Prince Harry's reported $100K deal for Princess Diana MasterClass sparks 'cash grab' claims from royal experts
articles.summary: Royal experts debate whether Prince Harry is a "grief grifter" as he discusses Princess Diana's death in a new paid MasterClass course on loss.
articles.body: Prince Harry has spent years publicly unpacking his grief over the death of his mother, Princess Diana. But his latest revelations have sparked renewed skepticism among royal experts. The Duke of Sussex opened up about how losing his mother when he was 12 affected his life in a new MasterClass course titled "Redefining Grief: Building Resilience Through Loss," which debuted Oct. 8. In the course, Harry spoke with neuroscientist and grief expert Dr. Mary-Frances O'Connor about how grief can affect the brain and body. PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE FEEDING THE 'PUBLICITY MACHINE' DESPITE PRIVACY DEMANDS: EXPERT The Daily Mail reported that Harry pocketed $100,000, plus a share of subscription revenue for his class. A source told the outlet, "I'd encourage everyone to watch it before casting any judgment," adding that he should not be criticized at length for "speaking from the heart." Forbes previously reported that most MasterClass instructors get at least $100,000 and a share of at least 30% of revenue. The Daily Mail reported that a spokesperson confirmed Harry was paid by MasterClass but declined to comment further. Past stars featured on the platform include Martin Scorsese, Gordon Ramsay and Hillary Clinton, among others. Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell and MasterClass for comment. Several royal experts told Fox News Digital that Harry's decision to repeatedly revisit his grief through books, interviews and media projects has fueled debate over whether the 42-year-old is profiting from the tragedy he shares with his brother, Prince William, who has largely chosen to grieve outside the spotlight. WATCH: PRINCE HARRY'S REPORTED PRINCESS DIANA MOVIE PROJECT SPARKS CONTROVERSY "Prince Harry has spoken extensively about his emotional scars and unresolved grief surrounding the death of his mother," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "However, Harry continuously paints himself a victim," Chard said. "Blame always falls on someone else. He realizes people's interest in Diana and, let's not forget, it makes a quick buck. It's seen as a cash grab, cashing in on his mother's death. It plays into the reported title 'Grief Grifter.'" "The public understands the heartache Harry and William must have endured after their mother passed away," Chard said. "Grief affects people in different ways, and both boys endured divergent paths of grief." According to People magazine, MasterClass approached Harry about developing a class on grief in 2025. The course was filmed in California during the summer of 2026, before Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, traveled back to the U.K. People reported that the course, released ahead of World Mental Health Day on Oct. 10, supports two charities: Scotty's Little Soldiers, a U.K. organization that helps children and young people whose parents died during or after service in the British Armed Forces, and Comfort Zone Camp, a U.S. nonprofit that provides bereavement camps for grieving children. According to The Times, William does not plan to make a film about Diana to mark the 30th anniversary of her death in 2027, in part to avoid further conflict with Harry. The outlet also reported that William has declined several offers to make or appear in documentaries about his mother. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Meanwhile, Harry is considering several projects to mark the 30th anniversary of Diana's death, according to People magazine. While several ideas are under discussion, the outlet reported that no documentary has been finalized or confirmed. Several sources told People that Harry has reached out to family members and friends of his late mother. The class also arrived just weeks after Princess Diana's younger brother, Charles Spencer, released his memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." At the beginning of the course, Harry recalled his reaction to learning of his mother's death. "I didn't cry when I was told my mom died, only at her burial, and then not again for nearly two decades," he said, as quoted by People. "I was convinced that was strength, but it wasn't. It was a 12-year-old boy with no permission to fall apart and no roadmap for how to heal." "You would think I had the best help in the world," Harry said. "I'm a prince for God's sake. But I was still grieving and didn't have any place to put those feelings." In his 2023 memoir, "Spare," Harry wrote that his father, King Charles III, didn't hug him after telling him Diana had died. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Pa didn't hug me," Harry wrote. "He wasn't great at showing emotions under normal circumstances. How could he be expected to show them in such a crisis? His hand did fall once more on my knee, and he said, 'It's going to be OK.' That was quite a lot for him. Fatherly, hopeful, kind. And so very untrue." For some royal experts, however, the issue isn't whether Harry has a right to discuss his grief, but his decision to repeatedly revisit it publicly. "Sadly, Harry hasn't dealt well at all with his grief," British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. Fordwich echoed Chard's criticism, saying Harry has faced accusations of being a "grief grifter" for repeatedly discussing his mother's death through public projects that could generate revenue. "What mother would want her child to be miserable and mourning so many years later?" Fordwich asked. Other royal commentators see Harry's decision differently. Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital that Harry is using his platform to raise awareness of mental health issues and encourage others to discuss their experiences and seek help. "I feel this is not a ploy on his part to create attention or sympathy from the public," Turner said. "I see it as an act of bravery on his part to distance himself from former royal trappings and show himself as most people see him: a man of the people." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Harry also said he spent years feeling that experiencing happiness would mean betraying his mother's memory. "I'd spent so long emotionally numb, to a large extent, because I felt disloyal and guilty for the possibility of being happy and joyful without her," Harry said. "I felt like I had to be sad, and I had to be emotionally numb in order to prove to her that I missed her." "But the reality is, what I discovered was actually she just wanted me to be happy," Harry said. "And that was a huge mental shift for me. It freed me, and it gave me a whole different outlook on life." In the course, Harry also described his experience after moving to Canada with his wife, Meghan Markle, and their son, Prince Archie, in late 2019. The couple stepped back from their roles as senior working royals in 2020, citing intrusive British media coverage and a lack of support from the palace as reasons for their departure. Harry said he experienced an "adrenaline crash." "We moved to Canada to get some space away from everything, just to be able to think," Harry said. "Being in Canada, away from the stressful environment where presumably my body was just pumped full of adrenaline, within two or three days, I experienced this adrenaline crash — something that I'd never experienced before." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It was as if I needed stress in order to get the adrenaline to make my brain function because I became useless around the house," Harry said. "I actually slipped into depression for about two weeks and I felt like I couldn't function without adrenaline." Harry's disclosure that he experienced depression shortly after leaving royal life caught Chard's attention. "The new narrative that he was depressed for a couple of weeks after leaving the British royal family is slightly suspect and does not resonate with his 'Freedom Flight,'" Chard said. "Harry wears his heart on his sleeve, and many doubt he'd forgotten to state this information in his previous memoir, documentaries and interviews." "This is definitely new information and slightly changes the narrative," Chard said. Harry also said that carrying out royal duties triggered anxiety and panic attacks. "There was a time where public engagements just created absolute panic right from beginning to end," Harry said. "The panic was having to put my suit, jacket, and tie on and suddenly feel suffocated. The panic was going from A to B, getting out of the car in front of all the cameras and the clicks. PRINCE WILLIAM ‘INCANDESCENT WITH ANGER’ AT PRINCE HARRY AS DIANA ANNIVERSARY DEEPENS ROYAL RIFT: PIERS MORGAN "I started to realize that I had become seriously depleted when just putting a simple dress shirt on — the tightening of the collar — literally felt like I was suffocating, and I would be experiencing panic attacks just in the car on the way to work," Harry said. "And that's when I realized, OK, there's something bigger, there's something else that you need to look into here." Royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital he believes Harry will continue discussing Diana's death if he moves forward with a documentary about his mother. "There is no doubt he is likely to continue emphasizing his vulnerability after Princess Diana's death," Fitzwilliams said. "We saw the emotional Harry on MasterClass, yet again." Harry also credited therapy with helping him confront grief he had carried for decades. "I learned more about myself in two or three sessions than I had done in 20 years," Harry said. "First of all, she helped me accept and acknowledge that I was grieving and that it was okay to grieve and that what happened to me was really quite hard." Nearly three decades after Diana's death, Harry and William continue to take different approaches to honoring their mother's memory — one through public revelations, the other largely away from the spotlight.

articles.title: Exmoor Dark Skies Festival: Event celebrates 10th anniversary
articles.summary: Stargazers are preparing to enjoy an annual festival that celebrates the beauty of the night sky.
articles.body:
Stargazers and astronomers are preparing to enjoy a festival that celebrates the beauty of the night sky.

The annual Exmoor Dark Skies Festival is being held from 16 October to 1 November and this year is its 10th anniversary.

Taking in villages and towns surrounding Exmoor National Park, the event offers walks, talks and shows - putting the dark, clear, night sky into full focus.

But what is the event all about - and what is behind its success over the past decade?

'Strong and brave' heritage railway chairman dies

Police warn online grooming of children is 'getting easier'

Top autumn walks as leaves expected to be more vibrant

The event celebrates the national park's status as a Dark Sky Reserve.

Granted by the International Astronomical Union in 2011, the status aims to safeguard the right of any citizen to enjoy the night sky by helping to limit light pollution.

Festival organiser Julie Colman said: "We bring together lots and lots of events across the two-week period, celebrating the skies, the wildlife, the wellbeing elements of it."

There are about 80 events taking place across the park, from moonlit swimming and astronomy sessions, to bioluminescence walks and planetarium shows.

Colman said there is "very little light pollution on Exmoor", adding it "enables the dark to be really dark with none of the pollution impacting".

"In the core of the reserve, there's an area where there is no light at all in a huge area - and that just makes the sky so much clearer and you're able to see some incredible constellations.

"You can see the Milky Way - it really is fantastic."

Photographs taken during previous dark skies events show incredibly clear views of the stars against a clear, dark backdrop.

The National Park said it designed the event in 2017 to, in part, help local businesses towards the end of the traditional tourism season.

In Dunster, on the edge of Exmoor, the Yarn Market Hotel manager Antony Brunt said in recent years, "it has become much more widely known - and now we literally have people ringing us up to book".

The hotel hosts special trips during the festival, led by a local astronomer, and runs visits to various sites and events across the park.

Brunt said the festival brings in people from all over the UK, adding: "It's getting to a quieter time of year and these people, they really enjoy coming down.

"We have a group that come each year, in fact, twice a year. For people to come regularly twice a year to the same hotel, they must be enjoying the stargazing part of the weekend."

The growing popularity of the festival meant that many events sold out before the opening day.

articles.summary: Lee Marvin's iconic Tucson estate, once sold for $1.825 million, is back on the market for $5.75 million after major renovations. The stunning property features extensive upgrades including a chef's kitchen, luxury primary suite, and spectacular outdoor amenities.
articles.body: Lee Marvin, who is best known for his work in ‘Paint Your Wagon,' ‘Point Blank,' ‘The Dirty Dozen,' and ‘The Twilight Zone,' bought out his iconic Tucson estate in 1975. The prestigious Catalina Foothills Estate is one of the most iconic spaces in the Hollywood star’s real estate portfolio. The massive 7,261-square-foot property was once home to the iconic star up until his passing in 1987. While the home had remained in his family for years, it was later sold off in 2021, restored, and recently put up on the market again.In 1975, Lee Marvin bought his iconic Tucson estateThe property, according to reports shared online by Homes.com, came under the Oscar-winning actor’s ownership in 1975. Designed by the famous architect Josias Joesler in 1936, it is located at 5055 N. Calle La Vela. The stunning Tucson property was built with classic mud-adobe and masonry stucco that was popular at the time of its construction, while also featuring a courtyard-centered layout with an expansive fountain, exposed beam ceilings, mission-tile porches, and scored concrete floors.In 2021, Lee Marvin’s Tucson property was finally sold for USD 1.825 millionFor four decades, the 4.12-acre property stayed with the Marvin family well after the ‘Point Blank’ actor’s passing. However, in 2021, the space was sold off for USD 1.825 million and underwent major renovations and reconstructions guided by the new owners, who have not been listed anywhere.The property now includes seven bedrooms and six and a half bathrooms, including the main residence and guest quarters. The kitchen and dining area were fully renovated after it was sold and were turned into a professional chef’s kitchen. The space now features honed marble surfaces, custom cabinetry, Sub-Zero refrigeration, and a Wolf gas range. The space also has a spacious living room, den, and primary suite, all of which have four fireplaces distributed throughout them.One of the specialties of the primary suite of Marvin’s former property includes vaulted/cathedral ceilings, a personal wet bar, double vanity, soaking tub, and custom walk-in closet space. Following its renovations, a lot of features were added and improved. These included a separate detached guest house, along with a studio room, and a 3-car detached garage. Lastly, the vast property also has a lot of outdoor features, including a private swimming pool, tennis court, custom pavers, and natural desert landscaping, which offer the residents stunning and panoramic views of the Catalina Mountains.Lee Marvin’s former property has now come back on the market for USD 5.75 millionOn the listing website Trulia, it was revealed that the property, which belonged to Lee Marvin and was his beloved home until his passing, is now back on the market. It has been listed for sale at the asking price of USD 5.75 million. As of right now, the property is still on the market for sale.Who is Lee Marvin?Born on February 19, 1921, Lee Marvin was one of the most famous stars of his time in the Hollywood industry and was best known for his ‘tough guy’ roles. His career spanned from 1951 to 1986, during which time he worked on more than 130 feature films, as well as TV shows. Before he became an acting icon, Marvin was enlisted in the US Marine Corps during World War II. He served as a scout sniper in the Pacific Theater and was severely wounded in the Battle of Saipan, earning a Purple Heart. Some of his most well-known works include ‘Cat Ballou,' ‘The Big Heat,' ‘The Wild One,' ‘The Dirty Dozen,' and many others.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted.
