articles.title: In 1988, Denzel Washington bought a Colonial Revival house built in 1940; years later, it was sold for USD 4.445 million in 2019
articles.summary: Explore the fascinating history of Denzel Washington's Colonial Revival mansion in Los Angeles, from its original architect Paul Revere Williams to its resale for USD 4.445 million in 2019. Discover the rich Hollywood history and preserved features of this iconic home.
articles.body: Denzel Washington invested USD 1.1 million in the beautiful Colonial Revival mansion that he bought in Los Angeles back in 1988. The stunning residence, which has a rich Hollywood history even before the famed actor bought it out, was resold by Washington and his wife, Pauletta, in 2000 for USD 1.9 million.In 1988, Denzel Washington bought the stunning LA propertyAccording to reports shared online by the Los Angeles Times, the property that Washington bought in 1988 was originally built and designed in 1940 by Paul Revere Williams, one of the biggest and pioneering African American architects who shaped mid-century Southern California luxury and designed homes for clients like Frank Sinatra, Lucille Ball, and Cary Grant.About the interior of Denzel Washington’s former LA homeThe iconic property, which spans two stories, covered 6,300 square feet on an expansive double lot spanning more than half an acre. The house was preserved to keep its 1940s charm alive, with the original moldings, built-in cabinetry, picture windows, and dual fireplaces in the living and family rooms, all still in their original places. The outer grounds across the entire property feature landscaped gardens, a swimming pool with a cabana, a koi pond, and a separate detached guest house.The 1940s colonial Los Angeles home’s celebrity historyThe 1940s home already had a rich Hollywood history before Washington. The first famed star who stayed in the LA home was Leon Errol. He was a popular and well-known comedian and actor for whom the house was originally built in 1940. Errol was best known for his work in ‘The Girl from Mexico,' ‘Joe Palooka, Champ,' ‘One Heavenly Night,' and ‘The Invisible Man's Revenge,' among others.Next up, the house went under the ownership of William Holden and Brenda Marshall. The Oscar-winning actor and his actress wife lived in the home from 1947 to 1959. During their tenure in the house, they notably hosted the wedding reception for Ronald and Nancy Reagan there in 1952.The LA home was resold at USD 4.445 million in 2019According to Mansion Global, in 2000, Washington sold the property to television writer-producer Brenda Hampton, who stayed in the house, renovated it, and later sold it herself in 2019. Originally, the sale value back in 2000 for the LA residence was USD 1.9 million; however, Brenda sold the space for USD 4.445 million back in 2019. Currently, no records of the current owner have been made publicly available.Who is Denzel Washington?Denzel Washington was born on December 28, 1954, in Mount Vernon, New York. articles.standfirst: Una información del periodista especializado Javi Oliveira
articles.summary: Una información del periodista especializado Javi Oliveira
articles.body: Ha sido una de las imágenes más virales de las últimas horas. Sin venir a cuento, los espectadores de ‘El sótano Club’ de TEN, vieron como su presentadora, Alba Carrillo, abandonaba rápidamente el plató ante la mirada atónita, preocupada e incómoda de los contertulios. No solo lo hacía de manera improvisada, sino que se mostraba altamente afectada por lo ocurrido. Momentos después, las redes sociales se inundaban con preguntas al respecto de los motivos que han derivado en que Carrillo abandone de esta manera el programa de TEN. Todos se calmaron cuando esta aparecía horas después en el estreno del nuevo canal de television, La Séptima, donde ya se conoce que colaborará como presentadora de programas del canal. En esta presentación, Carrillo parecía estar completamente recompuesta del sofoco que horas antes había protagonizado en ‘El sótano Club’. Ahora, todo parece indicar que esta emoción de la presentadora podría estar ligada a la despedida de la casa que la acogió durante tanto tiempo, ya que este viernes, 16 de octubre, iba a ser su último día como trabajadora para TEN TV, pero finalmente, el programa se ha cancelado. Y es que fue la propia presentadora la que comunicó, en el acto de presentación de La Séptima, los motivos que habían derivado en que esta saliese emocionada del programa, destacando que prefería estar al 100% en un programa y no a medias en dos espacios. La propia cuenta de TEN TV ha anunciado mediante un comunicado en sus redes sociales que hay un inminente “cambio de programación” y que “necesitamos algo de tiempo para trabajar en ellos”, refiriendose a los cambios que se van a producir en el espacio. Periodistas especializados como Javi Oliveira destacan que no ha sido despedida, sino que “ha decidido en el último momento dejar ‘El sótano club’, dejando tirados a todos”. “Hubo discusiones y malos rollos”, anuncia el periodista. “Hoy viernes iban a hacer el programa con normalidad, pero el equipo ha decidido no hacerlo para evitar una bronca”, afirma Javi Oliveira. “Se ha ido dejando tirado el programa, bloqueando a todos sus compañeros y Andy (de Andy y Lucas) se queda colgado”, ha sentenciado destacando que la presentadora ha salido mal de sus periodos en Telecinco, TVE y TEN.

articles.summary: Joe Manganiello's memoir "Bloodlines" reveals a voodoo curse claim, a $200,000 surrogate attempt and Tom Cruise's alleged role in his career.
articles.body: Joe Manganiello released his new memoir, "Bloodlines," which is already receiving a lot of buzz online. From revealing details about his divorce from Sofía Vergara, the seven-year long mystery illness that nearly took his life, and Tom Cruise's alleged involvement in the star being nixed in the "Reacher" series, below are the biggest bombshells from "Bloodlines: A Memoir." Their divorce was finalized in 2024. JOE MANGANIELLO DENIES SOFIA VERGARA’S CLAIM MARRIAGE ENDED BECAUSE HE WANTED A BABY: ‘SIMPLY NOT TRUE’ In his memoir, Manganiello detailed that he proposed to her in Spanish in Kauai, Hawaii and the next year they were married. They planned on starting a family. "She told me that when we first met, she wasn’t thinking about having more children, but she had sworn that if she ever remarried and her husband wanted kids, she’d do it," Manganiello wrote. "It was clear right away how we felt about each other, so at the urging of her doctor, before we were even engaged, we began trying via IVF." Manganiello said that after two years of trying to have a child, they were unsuccessful. The former couple even entertained the idea of having a surrogate, but $200,000 later, they decided it was not the right time due to Manganiello's "mystery illness." Manganiello says his illness changed the marriage A year after the couple tied the knot, Manganiello was admitted into the hospital for two months straight. "To visit me, Sofía had to lie down out of sight in the back of her assistant’s car, until they were sure they had lost the paparazzi, before heading to the hospital where she would disguise herself in a wig and hat and sneak in through the loading dock," Manganiello wrote. It was Vergara who made the lifesaving decision to have the doctor's remove Manganiello's large intestine so he would survive. "While I was under, they called Sofía, who, as my next of kin, had to choose what she thought I would want the doctors to do. She made the brutal but lifesaving decision to allow my entire large intestine to be removed and a hole to be cut into my abdomen to divert my small intestine." Manganiello credits his illness for contributing to his marriage with Vergara falling apart. "I started to live separately on the opposite side of the house during the day, and with the loss of my enthusiasm for life and the death of the dream of her and me becoming parents together, the fire between us began to go out," he said, referring to the period after he was released from the hospital. Mystery illness and voodoo curse Manganiello was admitted into the hospital for two months straight after a year of symptoms from his "mystery illness." He lost 60 pounds in two weeks after having his large intestine removed to save his life. In his memoir, he wrote that a Cuba-based shaman told him he was "sick" and "something is wrong with his intestines." At the time, Manganiello said members of his close family did not even know the extent of his illness and gave Vergara a "side-eye" that was "equal parts fear, anger, and disbelief." The shaman then said that an ex from Vergara's past who still had romantic feelings for her put a curse on Manganiello. "'Someone from your past is still in love with you. He put a voodoo curse on your husband. He did it in New Orleans,'" Manganiello recalled the shaman telling him. He continued, "'Your husband needs to be cleansed and protected. I can do this. I can help him. But I need to see him for two days, and I cannot come to the United States. Can he meet me somewhere else? I could meet him in Ecuador.'" Manganiello was stunned by the shaman's comments. "I looked at Sofía, trying to comprehend how the f–k this guy could possibly know any of this," he wrote. "None of this had been mentioned in the press. No one knew." Manganiello began raking his brain, trying to figure out what ex it could be. He eventually believed it could have been "the guy she was with right before me." Vergara and Nick Loeb called off their engagement in 2014. That same year, Vergara began dating Manganiello. He wrote in his memoir that Loeb suffered a "horrendous car wreck" while he was dating Vergara and began to question if his ex-wife was the cursed one. "The thought crossed my mind maybe it was Sofía who was cursed, cursed by some man in her past who couldn’t have her, so he put some sort of hex on her so that for the rest of her life, she’d transmit it to any man who got together with her," Manganiello wrote. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE He continued, "I was fully aware of how crazy it was for me to seriously entertain thoughts this bizarre, but then again, how did the shaman know all of that about me?" Loeb shared a statement with Page Six after learning of Manganiello's accusations. "I pray they find Jesus — not another shaman," he told the outlet. The divorce Manganiello recounted the moment he told Vergara that he was "leaving the marriage." "After she left for a vacation in Italy with her friend, I found a place to live, got the keys, and ordered a bed and a TV to be delivered that weekend. I then had everything I owned packed up and moved out," he wrote. Manganiello clarified that it was only after he moved out of their home in Beverly Hills to a new place in Venice Beach that he filed for divorce. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS He also wrote about a $500,000 loan he took from Vergara to prevent the bond company from taking over the 2019 movie, "Bottom of the 9th," after "a major budgetary error was discovered headed into the postproduction phase." "Because I was also the producer and star, I felt as though saving the film was my responsibility, and when I began the process of lining up a bank loan, Sofía offered to lend me the money with 0 percent interest," Manganiello wrote. "I’d never in my life taken a dime from anyone I’d ever dated, let alone her, but I swallowed what little of my pride I had left and accepted." At the time of the divorce, he still owed Vergara $400,000. He disputes claims about why they split Manganiello addressed the comments Vergara made about their divorce in the media, and called them "annoying" in his memoir. "But at the end of the day, they didn’t really matter as long as they didn’t ultimately hurt my career," he emphasized. Manganiello made some harsh claims about Vergara's departing words to him. "What bothered me more were the things said in a surgical attempt to hurt me as I walked out the door. She told me that I was wrong, that I wasn’t healthy after all, and that I was going to get sick again. She also let me know that in her opinion, no one was going to love me when they found out the full extent of what I had," he wrote. "That was the last time I ever spoke to her," he clarified. Tom Cruise speculation Manganiello accused Vergara's ex, Tom Cruise, of getting in the way of his involvement in the Prime series, "Reacher." In his memoir, Manganiello wrote that Amazon executives were set on him for the role of Lee Child, but the part suddenly went to someone else. He suspects Cruise was involved in that decision. Cruise, "an executive producer [on the show], could have potentially come in over the top and vetoed my being cast on account of Sofía," Manganiello wrote. articles.title: 'The film of the year': Critics rave about Nathan Fielder's 'masterpiece' Elizabeth Holmes movie
articles.summary: Filmed largely in secret, "You Can See Everything" takes viewers inside the life of the Theranos founder before prison.
articles.body:
Nathan Fielder's new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes is being hailed by critics as one of the year's best movies.

You Can See Everything , in theaters now, follows the Theranos founder in the weeks leading up to her 2023 imprisonment and the years that followed, after she was convicted of defrauding investors in her blood-testing startup.

One critic said it should be considered alongside the documentary form's "all-time greats."

The film was made largely in secret over nearly four years, with its existence only revealed when it premiered at a surprise screening at the Telluride Film Festival in September.

Fielder, best known for the TV shows Nathan for You and The Rehearsal , has built a career around awkward encounters and elaborate social experiments. The new film was co-directed by Lance Oppenheim, who made the recent Robert Pattinson movie Primetime .

Oppenheim was reluctant to reveal much about the film ahead of its release, telling People , "I don't want to say anything that can skew people's perception of it because I feel like it's one of those movies that the more clean slate you are, the better."

While the documentary has received overwhelmingly positive reviews, critics haven't agreed on everything. Here's what they liked about You Can See Everything — and where they felt it fell short.

What did critics like about 'You Can See Everything'?

You Can See Everything has received near-universal praise, making it one of the year's best-reviewed movies so far.

The Daily Beast called the film an "all-time great mind-melter," with its critic Nick Schager adding, "It's not just the film of the year — it's a documentary that stands shoulder-to-shoulder with the form's all-time greats." Similarly, Vulture called it "the movie of the year" and suggested Holmes was "one of the greatest doc subjects of all time."

The Guardian 's five-star review hailed the movie as a "modern masterpiece of deceit" that lives up to the hype, adding that it is "somehow more shocking, twistier, thornier and revealing than billed."

Fielder is known for blurring the lines between reality and performance, and other reviews suggest the film takes a similarly unconventional approach. Variety called it "just about the furthest thing from a 'pure' documentary you've ever seen," while the Los Angeles Times said it was "far stranger than a conventional documentary."

TheWrap argued that the film "uncovers complex new layers to the Holmes saga," while praising it for transcending the documentary form and being "impossibly involving" — a "documentary to end all documentaries."

Deadline 's critic, Pete Hammond, said it was "unlike any I have ever seen" due to the level of access given to the subjects. Vanity Fair said it was "full of unexpected twists and turns and shocking reveals," with Fielder and Oppenheim having "incredible access" to Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans.

The A.V. Club called it "a stunning reevaluation of what documentaries are capable of," adding, "It's a wild ride, filled with more twists and turns than your average thriller."

What didn't critics like about 'You Can See Everything'?

Despite the glowing reviews, some critics had reservations about the documentary's nearly three-hour runtime and Fielder's treatment of Holmes.

The Washington Post 's Shane O'Neill acknowledged that the film needs its lengthy runtime, but said it "doesn't fly by." "Even for the most hardcore cringe aficionado, it's a tough watch," he wrote, adding that by the second hour, he had developed a stomachache from the discomfort of watching it.

O'Neill warned that viewers unimpressed by the trailer were "in for a long night," though he ultimately called the film a masterpiece.

The New Yorker 's Richard Brody questioned Fielder's treatment of Holmes, arguing that his confrontational style gives his work "an air of cruelty." Brody pointed to Fielder's "sarcastic" exchanges with Holmes, including moments when he "embarrasses" her in front of her parents.

Brody also criticized the film's editing, arguing that it "precludes the tension of continuous unfoldings." Nevertheless, he praised the finished documentary as "strangely, poetically, poignantly beautiful."

The trailer shows Fielder arriving at Holmes and Evans's home with a suitcase, ready to move in while filming the couple. "Does any part of you worry about me being here 24/7?" Fielder asks Holmes, to which she replies, "I don't think so."

"Well, what if I see something that makes you look bad?" he asks. Holmes smiles but does not answer.

Fielder asks Evans whether he was worried Holmes was "scamming" him when they first met. "A hundred percent, but what did she have to gain from me?" Evans replies.

"Well, isn't your family rich?" Fielder asks. "Yeah," says Evans, an heir to a hotel group. "I think there are a lot of different levels of wealth." Evans adds that he has "never" suspected Holmes of lying to him.

Fielder tells Holmes directly that he has a "weird feeling there's some things I'm not seeing." "It's because I don't have anything to hide," she replies.

The trailer ends with Holmes saying, "It took me a really long time to be OK with letting someone see me cry." A single tear then rolls down her cheek.

articles.title: In 2009, an Austrian investor bought Arnold Schwarzenegger’s childhood home for USD 656,000; years later, it is now a museum dedicated to the actor’s journey
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring story of Arnold Schwarzenegger, from his humble beginnings in Thal, Austria, to becoming a global icon. Explore the newly established museum dedicated to his life and career, showcasing memorabilia and highlights of his journey as an actor, bodybuilder, and politician.
articles.body: Arnold Schwarzenegger grew up in Thal, a small village located near Graz in Austria, and had humble beginnings. The actor grew up in a strict, low-income household where his father worked as a local police chief. He remained ambitious for his future and is now one of the biggest and most beloved icons worldwide. While the actor has moved to a sprawling estate in the Brentwood neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, his roots in Thal remain strong, all thanks to an Austrian investor. The man bought the ‘Terminator’ actor’s childhood home at an auction all the way in 2009, and it has now been transformed into a museum for the star.About Arnold Schwarzenegger’s childhood home in ThalLocated at Linakstrasse 9 in Thal and originally built all the way back in 1806, it once used to be a forester's house for the Counts of Herberstein, according to The Daily Herald. Later, it was converted into the official residence for the local police commander of the area, who was Arnold's father, Gustav Schwarzenegger. He worked as the local police chief, and the Schwarzenegger family lived on the upper floor of the building. Another family occupied the ground floor of the space. The actor and politician lived in the house up until August 1966, when he moved out at the age of 19 to pursue his weightlifting career.Arnold Schwarzenegger’s childhood home went up for auction and was bought in 2009According to the outlet, in 2009, Austrian investor Christian Baha, who is the founder of the Vienna-based hedge fund, acquired the privately owned property at an auction for USD 656,000 at the time.Arnold Schwarzenegger’s childhood home is now a museumThe home, which was sold off in 2009, is now a museum entirely dedicated to the veteran star’s journey in the industry. The space explores his career as a weightlifter and an actor, as well as a politician, showcasing how he came to be. The official description on the museum’s official website reads, “Since 2011, visitors to the museum, formerly the forest lodge of the Counts of Herberstein, have been able to trace the beginnings and career of Austria’s most famous son. Numerous exhibits illustrate his extraordinary life story and the most important stages of his life, such as his childhood and youth, bodybuilding, film career, and time as governor. Experience Terminator & Co. up close and immerse yourself in the life of Arnold Schwarzenegger!” The space now holds memorabilia and items from his childhood days, mannequins of some of his most popular roles in Hollywood, and merch and collector's items that fans from all over the world can come and visit.The conversion of the residence into a museum was spearheaded by Peter Urdl, former mayor of Thal, who was also a childhood friend and schoolmate of Schwarzenegger. When the actor got to know of the idea, he personally contributed hundreds of items from his personal collection to be displayed at the museum, which has been all set in a chronological manner. Some of the things from his childhood that have been put up for display include his childhood bed, early drawings, and his first set of homemade training weights, along with trophy replicas and dumbbells as well.Lastly, to mark his time as a governor, the space also includes a replica of the governor's desk he used while serving as the 38th Governor of California from 2003 to 2011.Who is Arnold Schwarzenegger?Arnold Schwarzenegger is an Austrian-American actor, former professional bodybuilder, businessman, and politician. The Austrian star is 79 years old and has worked extensively across three different industries to create a name for himself. His entry into the entertainment industry started with his acting debut in the 1970 fantasy-comedy film ‘Hercules in New York.' Some of his other notable works include the ‘The Terminator’ franchise, ‘Conan the Barbarian,' ‘Total Recall,' 'Predator,' 'Commando,' ‘True Lies,' 'Twins,' and many others.Beyond acting, in 2003, he entered politics and was elected the 38th governor of California during a recall election. articles.title: New movies to watch this weekend: See 'You Can See Everything' and 'Whalefall' in theaters, rent or buy 'Practical Magic 2' stream 'Love of Your Life' on Prime Video
articles.summary: Plus, "Street Fighter" gets another big-screen adaptation, while new documentaries center on Norm Macdonald and the Wu-Tang Clan.
articles.body:
Welcome to Trust Me, I Watch Everything , a weekly guide to notable new movies opening or becoming available each Friday.

This week brings one of the buzziest releases of the year to the big screen: the only recently announced Elizabeth Holmes documentary from Nathan Fielder, You Can See Everything, which is as good as, if not better than, the early reviews indicated. Also out now: Whalefall and Street Fighter.

If you'd prefer a movie night at home, you can rent or buy Buddy, the bizarre horror movie about an evil children's TV show mascot, or Runner, the Alan Ritchson-Owen Wilson buddy action comedy you didn't know you needed.

And over on streaming, you'll find a pair of straight-to-streaming debuts in the Margaret Qualley romantic drama tearjerker Love of Your Life , and Sacrifice on Netflix . There are also a slew of interesting documentaries newly available.

The buzziest release: You Can See Everything

Why you should rush out and see it : You've likely never seen anything like You Can See Everything, a documentary that plays like a definitive statement on the unknowability of others and how one person's "truth" isn't necessarily … true. It implicates the documentary form itself as inherently manipulative and far from objective, as it attempts to extract honesty and authenticity from disgraced Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes.

You Can See Everything is the first feature film from Nathan Fielder, a comedian whose nonfiction comedy shows Nathan For You and The Rehearsal serve as a twisted form of anthropology as much as they do pure cringe comedy, all of it involving real people who know they're on television but not that they're on a comedy show. The film is co-directed by Lance Oppenheim, a 30-year-old documentarian whose first non-doc film is also in theaters now: the Chris Hansen movie Primetime .

The logline is this: About a month before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her family's every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. Fielder himself is featured on-camera nearly as much, if not more, than Holmes and her husband, Billy Evans, who is a whole other can of worms himself.

Fielder's awkward and invasive style provides for some wild moments. He and his film crew are actually living at Holmes's house, and there are as many laugh-out-loud bits as there are profoundly unsettling ones. You won't soon forget the beating of some eggs. A sequence in which Fielder shows Holmes, who claims that her extremely literal nature is the cause of the misunderstanding that others would call fraud, the famous Abbott and Costello "Who's on first?" comedy bit is simultaneously hilarious and illuminating, hands down one of the most memorable scenes I've ever seen in a documentary. Is semiotics really her problem?

The movie evolves into something even more fascinating as Fielder wrestles with Holmes and her insistence that she did absolutely nothing wrong and that her fall from grace is all just a huge misunderstanding. Ultimately, it seems to be playing with the idea that several things can be true simultaneously.

The action then shifts forward two years and becomes something completely different that people familiar with Fielder's work will instantly recognize: a meta deconstruction of the documentary form and the idea of performance.

The less said about the second half, the better, though it is some of the most enthralling cinema I've seen in a theater in ages. There was something extra special about experiencing a three-hour-long documentary with a packed house; everybody laughed at the same time and leaned forward in their seats together. The way the movie wants audiences to empathize with Holmes one minute and then take a step back to interrogate exactly why the filmmakers would show you that moment, is another layer, using form as function to underline its point.

You Can See Everything is a brilliant film that feels like it could, and should, become the first documentary ever nominated for best picture. It's an incredibly timely document of a post-truth society. The pairing of Fielder, known for his filmic manipulations, and Holmes, an alleged master manipulator now serving time, is a perfect match. You can see everything, but did you?

What other critics are saying : It's one of the best-reviewed movies of the year. AP's Lindsay Bahr aptly sums it up with "You want something you haven't seen before? Here it is." Amy Nicholson at the Los Angeles Times writes, "The biggest strike against Holmes is this documentary's very existence. Who on Earth would genuinely want Fielder, the human equivalent of a skunk, to crash their last moments with their loved ones as he does his darnedest to stink up the place?"

How to watch: You Can See Everything is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Why it's a mixed bag : " Austin Abrams gets into a situation " has become a movie genre unto itself, and mere weeks after the release of Resident Evil, he's gotten himself into another pickle.

Based on the book by Daniel Kraus, Whalefall is about a man who, following the death of his father, goes diving off the coast of California in search of his remains, only to be swallowed by a massive sperm whale. While trapped in its belly with only one hour of oxygen left, Jay realizes that the hard-earned lessons his father imparted may be the key to his escape.

Whalefall is at its best when it's focused on the aforementioned "Austin Abrams in a whale's stomach" situation; unfortunately, a good chunk of the runtime is spent on melodramatic flashbacks depicting Abrams' character's strained relationship with his late father, played by Josh Brolin. Both actors give it their all and are very good, but the movie is, frankly, boring in these sections, and there are too many of them.

Whenever we do get to the inside-the-whale action, it's intense and engaging and forces you, the viewer, to wonder what the hell you would do in such a nightmare scenario. The practical effects go a long way, including the whale-stomach set they built for Abrams to get lodged in. The specifics of the whale digestive system's inner workings are also appropriately gross and scary. There's skin-burning acid in there!

Whalefall coasts on the promise of its premise just enough to eke out a recommendation despite being a bit underwhelming whenever the innards of a whale aren't onscreen.

What other critics are saying: They like it well enough. Nick Schager at the Daily Beast calls it a "biblical calamity that plays out in giddily squishy and stifling fashion" that "proves amusing genre pulp." The Guardian's Ben Lee, however, wasn't sold. "Flipping between a family drama of soul-searching and hackneyed advice-giving ('Survivors survive!') and the more immediate 4DX-suited rush of thrashing, squelching, splashing and panicking makes Whalefall a disorienting and frustrating experience," he writes.

How to watch: Whalefall is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Why it's a mixed bag: The maximalism is appreciated in Street Fighter, which unfortunately has far too much plotting for a movie based on a coin-operated arcade fighting game.

Whenever it gets down to business with its cartoonish violence — sometimes literally rendered in animated form, so often that you leave wondering why they didn't just do a cartoon movie instead — it delivers on the promise of over-the-top antics. It's loud, it's colorful and the score sounds like you're playing an old 8-bit game. The vibes feel right for the '90s arcade energy they're after.

The problem is that Street Fighter spends way too much time spinning its wheels, setting up its story, characters and their motivations. These are all basic elements required of most movies, to be sure, but ones that, I can assure the filmmakers, nobody cares all that much about in this specific movie.

The plot: In 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu and Ken Masters are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past.

The fights, unfortunately, feel more like afterthoughts. Hilariously, much like the Mortal Kombat adaptation from a few years ago, which just got a sequel I've already forgotten entirely, this movie has a perfect premise for "endless satisfying fight scenes" but fails to deliver. There's a literal tournament where people fight each other, yet many fights occur offscreen or are "canceled" for plot reasons. It's bizarre that both big-budget fighting movie series prize "lore" and plotting over making sure the action sings.

Street Fighter fans may get a kick out of seeing these characters onscreen again — it's the third go at it, after the 1994 Jean-Claude Van Damme one, which was a hit, and the 2009 bomb Legend of Chun-Li — but more casual moviegoers looking for a good time may find themselves exhausted by it.

What other critics are saying: It's largely getting knocked out, but it has its defenders. Jake Coyle at the AP writes, "As much as you might think a Street Fighter movie, good or bad, would at least offer up some bluntly entertaining hand-to-hand combat, it's so messily plotted and chaotically conceived that it makes a game with six buttons seem comparatively artful." TheWrap's William Bibbiani, however, writes that "[Director Kitao Sakurai's] raw enthusiasm for making this goofy-ass action movie is infectious. I'm not sure Street Fighter meets any conventional standard of quality, but it's undeniably its own thing."

How to watch: Street Fighter is now playing in theaters nationwide .

The Devils : Controversial British filmmaker Ken Russell's 1971 masterpiece is getting a wide release in its uncensored, NC-17 form for the first time. In the film, a charismatic 17th-century French priest (Oliver Reed) becomes the target of a sexually obsessed nun's (Vanessa Redgrave) witchcraft accusations, which corrupt church and state officials are all too happy to exploit.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ The movie was banned or censored in many countries due to its extreme depiction of religious blasphemy, graphic violence and sexual hysteria involving possessed nuns. The fact that you can now go see this at an AMC or Regal at the local mall is remarkable, and a major win for cinephiles who've only seen censored versions over the years. Get tickets.

Sense and Sensibility : A new take on Jane Austen's iconic novel, this is a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles . Get tickets.

Why you should see it : Casper Kelly, the guy famous for the viral Too Many Cooks bizarro comedy sketch and the Adult Swim Yule Log comedy-horror movies, makes his leap into the mainstream with this uniquely weird movie about a killer children's TV show mascot .

The premise is essentially: "What if a kid's show like Barney existed and Barney himself was an evil child murderer?" There are so many wild and fun ideas here, and the commitment to the bit is astounding, with incredible production design, costumes and invented characters.

I appreciated how out-there and surreal it gets, and particularly loved the mascot-centric gore. Cristin Milioti and Topher Grace star, while Keegan-Michael Key voices the titular Buddy.

What other critics are saying: They love him! Monica Castillo at AV Club writes, "Kelly recreates the look of these shows right down to their transition wipes and hip hop-lite choreography, but his darkest scares come from how someone who's not-so-nice gets away with bullying." TheWrap's Casey Loving , however, says, "Each time you think you're seeing the daylight of something potentially better to explore on the horizon, Buddy keeps dragging you back into the banal darkness. Like the kids, you deserve far better than whatever this lackluster production amounts to."

How to watch: Buddy is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Why you should see it: A mismatched buddy action-comedy starring Owen Wilson? Welcome back, early 2000s!

In the latest flick from Angel Studios, whose theatrical footprint has really grown this year , a former soldier and his unlikely partner become the targets of a ruthless cartel while racing to complete a critical medical delivery and save the life of a little girl.

To get a bit more specific, Owen Wilson plays a guy transporting an organ on ice with a very specific, fast-approaching expiration date. This makes the organ highly sought after by bad people, as it would fetch a ton of money on the black market … or maybe somebody has another reason for wanting it.

Ritchson plays the extremely reluctant courier hired to transport Wilson, and his dedication to getting the job done at any cost really helps power the movie. The action is exciting and fun, and the banter between Ritchson and Wilson is a hoot and harkens back to a bygone era of Wilson-starring action comedies. The plot is simply an excuse to showcase chase and action sequences, and the movie capitalizes on every opportunity, using some really clever camerawork.

I found Runner to be about 10,000% better than I expected based solely on its poster and premise. They should teach it in film school to show how even tired, formulaic material can work when it's handled with care and performed well. I was totally in the palm of the movie's hand. It's an unexpectedly crowd-pleasing charmer that I hope finds an audience and becomes a sleeper hit. It's a great time at the movies.

What other critics are saying : They're similarly impressed, relatively speaking. Todd Gilchrist at Variety writes, "This clunky vehicle doesn't transcend its limitations — Wilson and Ritchson's efforts are the duct tape holding it together — but it's much better than anyone could have expected." TheWrap's William Bibbiani calls it "the porridge Goldilocks ate, if Goldilocks loved kicking butt and taking names."

How to watch: Runner is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Hope: South Korean director Na Hong-jin is back with his first film since 2016's The Wailing, and it's a propulsive, wacky sci-fi creature feature that delivers blockbuster-sized spectacle in several memorable chase and/or action sequences. It's quite funny too, in ways both big and small. Hope ekes out a recommendation purely on the strength of its multiple extended set pieces, which are compelling before they start to get a bit repetitive. Read my full review here . Rent or buy .

Practical Magic 2 : Based on the fourth book in Alice Hoffman's popular series , the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all. In the original film, the Owens sisters discover a family curse that causes all the men they truly love to die, leading them to adopt two different lifestyles to cope with it. Now, this curse has passed down to Bullock's children, with disastrous consequences. I found the movie's use of the legacy-sequel framework uninspiring and was never fully engaged with the story, which I felt hewed too closely to the original, both in content and in the way it's all so loosely connected. The biggest issue, though, is with the screenplay. Read my full review here . Rent or buy .

📺 Movies newly available on streaming services you may already have

Why you should stream it: Warning: this isn't a romantic comedy; it's very much a romantic drama, even more of a tearjerker. It caught me off-guard, so I feel the need to warn readers.

After a chance encounter sparks a sweeping romance, Maya's future is suddenly upended, sending her on an unexpected journey to love and live again. In other words, it's a movie about a woman who falls in love, loses that love and then must learn to live with that fact and/or possibly love again.

Love of Your Life works well because the romance it depicts in the first act is so believable and charming that, when it turns out to be too good to be true, you feel that heartbreak viscerally. It's an honest movie with the unflattering reality of grief on full display, and I appreciated that it didn't take the easy "this is escapism" route and instead felt more grounded.

Love of Your Life gets a little schematic with its plotting eventually, but the ultimate message of learning to let go of your grief in order to live a full life is an important one, and the movie does a good enough job of getting there.

What other critics are saying: They like it, mostly! Variety's Guy Lodge writes, "For viewers after a grown-up romantic drama with equal, counterbalancing side servings of tearjerking trauma and glossy wish-fulfillment, Love of Your Life will handsomely suffice." The Hollywood Reporter's Jourdain Searles , however, calls it an "unpersuasive romantic travelogue."

How to watch: Love of Your Life is now streaming on Prime Video .

Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald : This Judd Apatow-directed documentary is a cleverly constructed profile of the beloved yet controversial comedian Norm Macdonald, told entirely through his own words, drawn from his many comedy sketches, stand-up bits, late-night talk show appearances and podcast gigs. It's a real treat for fans, especially as Apatow wrestles with who Macdonald, who died in 2021, really was, given he never shared too many personal details. Now streaming on Netflix .

Sacrifice : Netflix didn't provide early screeners for this one, but here's the logline: During a star-studded charity gala brimming with celebrities, billionaires and empty speeches, a movie star (Chris Evans) in the midst of an existential crisis is taken hostage by a radical warrior (Anya Taylor-Joy) and her devoted followers. Now streaming on Netflix.

Tenzing : This biopic starring Tom Hiddleston and Genden Phuntsok tells an incredible true story and renders it a total snoozefest. A determined man embarks on a high-stakes quest and defies seemingly impossible odds to fulfill his dream of being the first to reach the summit of Mount Everest. It never grabs you despite its subject matter. Now streaming on Apple TV .

The Death of Robin Hood : The Death of Robin Hood is so grim and bleak and dark that my initial response was simply to laugh at the audacity. In this gritty take on the man, myth and legend, we find Robin Hood (Hugh Jackman) grappling with his past after a life of crime and murder. He's also gravely injured after a battle he thought would be his last. In the hands of a mysterious woman (Jodie Comer), he is offered a chance at salvation. I understand the thematic idea at the center here: The harsh and brutal realities of life are often softened by the stories we tell. The violent truth is lost to history, and instead, we get legends about heroic figures. But something's off here. Read my full review here . Now streaming on HBO Max .

The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable : This wildly entertaining documentary explores how a Wu-Tang fan was able to infiltrate the group and become a member, and how he parlayed that position into being responsible for the Wu-Tang Clan's most widely publicized incident: the release, or lack of release, of their album Once Upon a Time in Shaolin. The album was conceived like this: What if Wu-Tang made an album but only released a single copy, thereby driving up its value and treating it like any other work of art that people would go see in person at a museum? The saga only gets crazier from there, and depending on your perspective, you'll either appreciate the man's audacity or blame him for the madness and publicity surrounding the album. It's an interesting story! Now streaming on Netflix .

That's all for this week! We'll see you next Friday, when the big releases are Clayface , Wildwood and Wicker.

articles.title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs moved to a new prison after reports of a luxury lifestyle behind bars
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Sean “Diddy” Combs has been moved to a federal prison in Pennsylvania after reports that the hip-hop mogul was living the high life and was i...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Sean "Diddy" Combs has been moved to a federal prison in Pennsylvania after reports that the hip-hop mogul was living the high life and was injured in a fight at his New Jersey lockup, a person familiar with the matter told The Associated Press on Friday.

The federal Bureau of Prisons is transferring Combs, 56, from FCI Fort Dix to FCI Allenwood Low, a low-security facility south of Williamsport and about 155 miles (250 kilometers) west of New York City, the person said. The person was not authorized to speak publicly and did so on condition of anonymity.

The Bureau of Prisons confirmed the move but provided no further details. The agency said it does not discuss conditions of confinement for anyone in its custody, including reasons for transfer, for privacy, safety, and security reasons.

"Decisions about inmate placement are made by the BOP, and we are not in a position to speak to the circumstances surrounding this transfer," said Combs' spokesperson, Juda Engelmayer. "Sean remains focused on moving forward, and we hope that his time at the new facility will be productive and without unnecessary disruption."

Combs is serving a four-year, two-month sentence for his conviction last year on prostitution-related charges for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters. The case featured harrowing testimony about violence and sex parties he called "freak-offs." It was a forceful reckoning for one of music and entertainment's most influential figures .

Last month, NBC News reported that Combs was continuing to enjoy aspects of his millionaire lifestyle at FCI Fort Dix, smuggling in Hennessy, having fellow inmates cook, clean, make his bed and give him massages, and using a contraband cellphone to view social media and an ex-girlfriend's nude selfies.

On Wednesday, TMZ reported that Combs was injured in a fight with another inmate at Fort Dix and had to be taken out of the prison for treatment. In a rare rebuttal, the Bureau of Prisons refuted TMZ's report, telling the AP: "The story you are referring to is false and did not happen."

In the wake of the NBC report, Combs was placed in the prison's special housing unit, a heavily secured part of the facility away from the general population, for inmates with disciplinary issues or security concerns. He has also been docked 41 days of good-conduct credit, pushing his release date back to March 2, 2028, according to the person familiar with the matter.

In April, the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals heard arguments in Combs' bid to overturn his conviction and sentence, which his lawyers argued was too harsh. The court has yet to rule.

articles.title: Nana Patekar's son Malhar talks about his parents' separation, his father's final moments before death: 'He was active, did two and a half hours of working out in a gym'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar’s estranged wife, Neelkanthi Patekar, was present at his funeral, bringing attention to their unusual relationship.
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar’s estranged wife, Neelkanthi Patekar, was present at his funeral, bringing attention to their unusual relationship. The couple tied the knot in 1978 and had two sons, Durvasa, who died in childhood, and Malhar. Although they had been living separately for 35 years, they never legally divorced. In a recent interview, their son and filmmaker Malhar Patekar recalled his father’s final hours and spoke about why his parents chose to remain married despite living apart.Recalling the circumstances surrounding his father’s death, Malhar told Hindustan Times, “Nana ji was in Goa, and my cousin Prasad who used to look into all his entertainment-related meetings, was sent off by him to Mumbai as he had to shoot for KBC Marathi with Madhuri ji (Dixit) in a day. Also, my other brother, Amay, only left after settling him upstairs in the house,” he said.Malhar also addressed speculation surrounding his parents’ relationship, emphasising that their emotional bond remained intact despite their decision to live separately. He said that outsiders’ perceptions did not reflect the closeness they shared as a family and questioned the tendency to judge relationships based on their social media presence.“When growing up as a kid, I imbibed a lot of strength and resilience from my parents. Also, whatever it looks like from the outside to people doesn’t matter to me; in reality, we as a family were strongly and emotionally connected even my uncle and cousins, for that matter. Mujhe sab ka pyar mila hamesha and that matters.”The filmmaker further spoke about the misinformation circulating about his family and clarified that his father was never alone during his final days. He also highlighted Nana’s remarkable fitness and active lifestyle, despite his age.“Itna sab kuch viral ho raha, woh kitna ghalat hai. Just because we don’t share family pics on Insta, that doesn’t mean we don’t bond. Even after parting ways, my parents were on a good note; 38-39 saal ka bond tha, and things are never what they might look like… The things I read usska jawab yeh hain ke woh akele nahi thhe, kabhi nahin thhe, nor was he unwell because we all never left his side; one of us was always with him. He was very active and doing two and a half hours of working out in a gym; youngsters nahin kar pate, that was his level of fitness.”Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 in Goa after suffering a cardiac arrest. articles.title: Zubeen Garg death case: Gauhati High Court grants bail to suspended DSP Sandipon Garg; prosecutor says. 'the court has not read out the full order'
articles.summary: The Gauhati High Court on Friday, October 16, granted bail to suspended Assam Police DSP Sandipon Garg in connection with the death of singer Zubeen Garg.
articles.body: The Gauhati High Court on Friday, October 16, granted bail to suspended Assam Police DSP Sandipon Garg in connection with the death of singer Zubeen Garg. Sandipon, a cousin of the late singer, had been arrested by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case.Court grants relief to Sandipon Zubeen GargA single bench of Justice Rajesh Mazumdar passed the bail order after hearing his petition. Speaking to ANI over the phone, Special Public Prosecutor Ziaul Kamar said, “Gauhati High Court has granted bail to Sandipon Garg, and the court has not read out the full order.”Amritprava Mahanta was the first to get bailLast week, on October 9, the same court granted bail to Amritprava Mahanta, a co-singer of Zubeen Garg. She became the first accused in the case to get bail. According to the prosecutor, the court released her on a bond of Rs 50,000. The SIT of the Assam Police had arrested her in 2025 after hours of questioning. She moved the High Court after her arrest, and the bail order followed.What happened to Zubeen Garg?The singer died in Singapore on September 19, 2025, in a scuba diving accident. This was a day before he was due to perform at the Northeast India Festival. Shyamkanu Mahanta, who has organised the festival since 2013, was also arrested after the singer’s death.Supreme Court asked Assam to ensure a speedy trialIn August, the Supreme Court told the Assam government to ensure a diligent and quick trial against Shyamkanu Mahanta, who faces criminal charges in the case. The State informed a bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and R Mahadevan that the trial was being held on a day-to-day basis. It added that several key witnesses were expected to depose in the coming weeks.Justice Nagarathna observed orally that the court was putting the State under pressure to keep the trial moving. She said the bench would review the progress when the matter came up again.Defence and State argumentsSenior advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Shyamkanu Mahanta, argued that the singer was an adult who had willingly boarded a boat and gone into the sea wearing a life jacket before drowning. He said Mahanta was not present at the time of the incident.Dave also questioned the allegation that Mahanta conspired to cause the death by not taking proper care of the singer or by giving him alcohol. He argued that Garg was an adult and Mahanta could not be blamed for his decision to drink.The State, however, maintained that the death was not an accident and said the prosecution had material pointing to a conspiracy.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Britney Spears: ‘You learn from it. You take that and you grow with it,’ a reminder that difficult experiences can make us stronger
articles.summary: Life does not always go as planned.
articles.body: Life does not always go as planned. Disappointment, broken trust and personal setbacks can leave people questioning themselves and struggling to move forward. However, difficult experiences can also help us understand our boundaries, recognise unhealthy patterns and approach the future with greater clarity. In a November 2001 interview published by Philstar, American pop star Britney Spears spoke about betrayal and personal growth.Motivational quote of the day by Britney Spears: “You learn from it. You take that and you grow with it.”What is the meaning of Britney Spears’ quote?The quote suggests that through painful experiences, one can reflect on their relationships with themselves and others. Although heartbreaking, the situations can teach people a lesson about trust, respect, and boundaries.One can reflect and mature from the incident, which implies that they truly accept what occurred and its effect on them. This does not necessarily mean dismissing the actions of people who hurt them. Instead, it implies being able to understand what the situation signifies and the red flags concerning future relationships with these individuals.Furthermore, the quote implies that although a disappointing experience may seem as the end of the road, it does not have to be a closure. Individuals can apply the acquired knowledge to future interactions to prevent similar occurrences and ensure healthier connections.Moreover, in some cases, it may signify accepting that one will not receive an apology or explanation from the person at fault. Therefore, people should allow themselves to process the incident and forgive those who wronged them to move on with their lives.Why is Britney Spears’ quote relevant today?Spears’ quote holds true meaning in today’s society because many people face disappointing situations and broken trust. Individuals often experience heartbreak and from family members, friends, coworkers, or public figures. It can be utterly disheartening, especially when one internalizes it, believing that all relationships are built on mistrust.The world has become so caught in the gram and the highlight of one’s life. However, people should realize that growth requires processing the setbacks and failures rather than dismissing them. Some of these situations can also be a source of valuable knowledge for future relationships. Although it may take time, the reflective process can enable individuals to identify what they will do differently with future partners.Additionally, the quote can signify recognizing the need for healthier boundaries. For instance, people can acknowledge their mistakes and prevent future conflicts with others. They may also choose to cut toxic people off to prevent ongoing emotional trauma. Furthermore, the saying can also be a reminder that although the incident may seem like the end of the road, there is always a new beginning.Early life of Britney SpearsSpears was born on December 2, 1981, in McComb, Mississippi, and raised in Kentwood, Louisiana. She discovered her passion for singing and dancing at a young age.At the age of 12, she began her television career by joining Disney Channel’s The All New Mickey Mouse Club in 1993. It marked the beginning of her stardom as she starred alongside future superstars Christina Aguilera, Justin Timberlake, and Ryan Gosling. It became the most-watched program on the network. However, it ended in 1994, and Spears continued her music career.Britney Spears’ rise to fameIn 1998, Spears rose to international fame with her debut single, “…Baby One More Time,” which reached the top of the Billboard Hot 100 in January 1999. Moreover, the music video came to define the late 90s pop culture. …Baby One More Time, her debut album, skyrocketed to the top of the charts in January 1999.She maintained her success with hits like Oops!… I Did It Again in 2000 and the Britney album in 2001. In 2003, she released In the Zone, which featured the chart-topping Toxic. Throughout her music career, Spears has released several successful albums and songs.What can we learn from Britney Spears’ quote?As mentioned, Spears’ quote serves as a somber reminder that every relationship, regardless of its outcome, can offer invaluable lessons. The quote encourages people to reflect on the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify what they will do differently in the future.However, it does not mean that the victim will completely dismiss what the perpetrator went through. Instead, they should focus on the aspects beyond their control and the behavior of the person at fault. Furthermore, one must understand that although the event may seem as the end of the road, there is always a new beginning. Therefore, people should not allow one incident to dictate the terms of all their relationships.Moreover, individuals need to give themselves time to process the event and move on. As such, the most crucial step is to allow oneself to grieve and reflect. However, it should not be an indefinite process since life goes on, and people need to continue loving and having relationships.Overall, Spears’ quote can be a helpful reminder during times of heartbreak and disappointment. It suggests that the incident is a valuable lesson in life that can increase one’s understanding of future relationships. articles.title: Billy Joel says he doesn’t know if he can perform on stage again due to brain disorder

articles.body: The Piano Man still wants to play, but it’s not clear when or if he’ll be able to sing again for, as the song goes, “the regular crowd.” Billy Joel, who has been battling a brain disorder for more than a year, says his doctor has advised him to remain on an extended break from what’s been his job for six decades — performing. “What the neurologist told me, every time you do a show, it’s like you’re getting a concussion,” Joel said in an interview Thursday with The Hollywood Reporter. Joel, who is 77, said the doctors are concerned performing before thousands of fans is taking a toll on him. “Rock ‘n’ roll is loud, man,” Joel said. “Rock ‘n’ roll made me deaf already. So it’s the lighting, the sound, the stress of the show, the audience, the energy of the performance. There’s a lot going on when you’re onstage.” “So they have to test me further to see if I can go back and do performing again, which I would like to be able to do,” he said. That said, Joel insisted his health “is good” and downplayed the effects of hydrocephalus, which he was diagnosed with in May 2025. It’s a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid builds up inside the skull and presses on the brain, according to the Cleveland Clinic. The condition is often treatable and sometimes reversible. “It used to be called water on the brain, so it affects your balance, it affects your memory, it affects your vision, your hearing,” he said. “But I’m OK. They call it a brain disorder, but it’s not that serious. It’s just something that affects your balance mostly.” Joel provided an update on his condition ahead of a Gooding Christie’s auction on Nov. 20 and 21 at the Javits Center in New York City where more than 70 motorcycles from his collection⁠ will be sold to the highest bidder. The money will go to support the Joel Foundation, which supports music education, women’s health programs, humanitarian relief and other causes. Joel said the hydrocephalus was a factor in his decision to part with his motorcycles, as the condition makes driving difficult. “I love motorcycles,” he said. “I love biking. I love driving. I love the anonymity of it. And I love the customization of these bikes, the modifications, the messing around with things. I was not a collector. I was actually a rider.” And being on a bike was also a source of musical inspiration, he added. “I mean, everything helps me to write songs,” Joel said. “But I wrote a song called, I think it’s called “You May Be Right,” where I said I even rode my motorcycle in the rain, which people from England would go, ‘Yeah, so what?’” Last month, Joel revealed he underwent brain surgery after he was diagnosed, because he didn’t want to lose his “marbles.” Speaking on his SiriusXM channel, Joel admitted he initially balked at going under the knife after being told that it involved having a surgeon “drill a hole through your skull” and “stick a shunt inside your brain.” “I didn’t want to do that,” Joel said. “But then I read up on it, and I realized it can help improve your balance and can help your memory. You know, I don’t want to lose my marbles.”

articles.title: Selma Blair Breaks Her Silence on Plane Arrest in Lengthy Statement from Rep: ‘Selma Did Not Intend to Harm Anyone’ (Exclusive)
articles.summary: “There is much more to this story than has been reported,” Blair’s spokesperson told PEOPLE
articles.body:
A representative for Selma Blair has shared a statement with PEOPLE regarding Blair's Oct. 11 arrest

The actress pleaded not guilty to two counts of second-degree assault following her arrest after an alleged altercation on a Delta Airlines flight

Blair "experienced a medical emergency on the flight" and "did not intend to harm anyone," her rep said in the statement

Selma Blair 's spokesperson has released a statement about the actress' recent arrest .

"Since Sunday night, the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline," said Blair's spokesperson in a statement shared exclusively with PEOPLE.

Blair, 54, was arrested at New York City's John F. Kennedy International Airport before being taken to a hospital following an alleged altercation with crew members on a Delta Airlines flight on Oct. 11. After appearing in court the next day and pleading not guilty to two counts of second-degree assault , the actress was released on bail.

"A handful of journalists have taken the time to report on Selma as a human being rather than a headline, and we are grateful to them," the statement continues. "But fair reporting has been the exception, and in the space left by our silence, speculation has hardened into something being treated as fact. We can, however, correct the record on a few points already in public circulation. Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight. There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone."

Blair publicly revealed her diagnosis of the chronic autoimmune disease multiple sclerosis in 2018.

In the statement shared with PEOPLE, the spokesperson adds that "the suggestion by anyone that Selma does not have multiple sclerosis is outrageous. Her diagnosis has been public since 2018. What Selma has been able to do physically in the years since is nothing short of a miracle. She still has bad days, and she lives with pain daily. Selma also has pseudobulbar affect, a neurological condition secondary to her MS, which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her. For the same reason, she travels with a service dog who doesn't leave her side, and the authorities took her dog from her."

Blair, the statement continues, "has worked on seven film and television projects in 2026 alone, only a couple of which have been announced. She has launched a skin care line, a clothing line, and a line of eye-glass readers, each built around the idea of beauty and utility for people whose bodies do not always cooperate. She remains a visible and relentless advocate for disability rights, for the MS community, and this year for the Jewish community in the face of rising antisemitism, including from the stage of the ADL's State of the Arts event at The Jewish Museum two weeks ago. Selma had never been arrested before Sunday night."

It concludes, "There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion."

Blair was accused of kicking a police officer repeatedly and a nurse in the chest aboard the Oct. 11 flight, according to a criminal court affidavit. Dispatch audio obtained by PEOPLE on Oct. 12 indicated that an emergency responder identified someone involved in the plane incident as injured with "some bite marks" on top of other minor injuries.

A spokesperson for the FBI confirmed on Oct. 12 that the agency is investigating the incident. Delta Airlines "has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," a spokesperson for the airline told PEOPLE.

Blair has faced several headline-making controversies through the years. In 2016, the Cruel Intentions star publicly apologized after causing a disturbance and being removed from a flight in Los Angeles following a trip to Cancun, Mexico.

In her 2022 memoir Mean Baby: A Memoir of Growing Up , Blair included a chapter titled "Bite Me," in which she wrote that in social settings she has bitten Sienna Miller , Seth MacFarlane and Kate Moss at separate times throughout the years.

Blair has also previously made headlines for making Islamophobic comments after leaving a since-deleted comment under an Instagram post that read, "Deport all these terrorist supporting goons. Islam has destroyed Muslim countries and then they come here and destroy minds. They know they are liars. Twisted justifications. May they meet their fate."

Blair later made an Instagram statement apologizing "with love and respect" for "inadvertently" making the comment after she "commented on a post by Abraham Hamra regarding two congress members who are against banning October 7th Hamas terrorists from entering the USA."

Following her Oct. 11 arrest, Blair is still expected to appear as scheduled at the upcoming 90s Con in Hartford, Conn., running Oct. 16–18.

articles.title: James McAvoy says ‘Band of Brothers’ co-star recruited fellow actors to bully him on set
articles.summary: James McAvoy revealed he was bullied on his first day filming "Band of Brothers" and named the co-stars who helped him through the experience.
articles.body: James McAvoy is getting candid about what it was like filming "Band of Brothers" and why it wasn't his best experience on a set. During a recent appearance on "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen," the actor was asked to rate his experience working on different projects, and when he was shown a picture of the show's cast, he said he was bullied during filming. "On my first day on set, there was a ton of actors," he began. "It was one of those scenes with everybody in it, and we’re all at a bar, and I had a scene. And all these guys were in it for nine months, 10 months, and they get one line in one episode, and one line 10 episodes later. They were all pissed. I come in for one episode, and I’ve got an arc and scenes. I’ve got tons of lines." When the photo, which featured many of his co-stars from the show, flashed on the screen, McAvoy got up to get a closer look, confirming that a specific actor was in the photo. DEBI MAZAR SAYS 'ENTOURAGE' SET 'GOT TOXIC' AFTER SHE RETURNED FROM HAVING HER SECOND DAUGHTER "So, one of the guys in that picture decided to bully me on my first day as a professional actor out of acting school," he said. "He got him and his buddies to just stand pointing at me and laugh at me for like three minutes." While he didn't name names, the photo featured Donnie Wahlberg, Kirk Acevedo, Scott Grimes, Neal McDonough, Adam James, Frank John Hughes, Philip Barantini and Ross McCall. The "X-Men: First Class" star added that not everyone on set participated in the bullying, saying Dexter Fletcher and Robin Laing "took me aside, and they were like, ‘Come hang with us, man.'" articles.title: Lucknow twirls to Garba beat, festive feast
articles.summary: Adani Times Garba Utsav 2026 in Lucknow blends dandiya dance, DIY crafts, food stalls and DJ MaskBox, with awards for best dancers and dress.
articles.body: Lucknow: Glittering faces, intricate braids and circles of dancers moving to the beat of dandiya sticks set the mood atAdani Times Garba Utsav 2026on Friday. With traditional outfits adding to the festive spectacle, the event brought together dance, food, craft and play, giving revellers plenty of reasons to dress up, let loose and make memories.Beyond the dance floor, visitors explored a carnival of hands-on activities. At the pottery corner, they tried their hand at shaping clay, while face art and intricate hair braiding helped them complete their festive looks.The viral falling-sticks challenge tested their reflexes, while DIY counters offered custom candles, crochet bouquets, phone charms and beaded bracelets.“I made a bracelet and picked a phone charm to match my outfit. It is a small souvenir from the evening,” said Ritika Sharma, a college student.Visitors also made the most of the event’s colourful backdrops, posing for pictures in coordinated outfits. For many, the evening was as much about creating content for Instagram as it was about dancing.“We planned our outfits beforehand and had a list of reels we wanted to shoot. Every backdrop gave us a different look, and we kept going back to the dance floor to capture the perfect clip,” said Riya Malhotra, a college student.The food stalls offered another reason to take a break between activities. Dabeli, Gujarati chaat, chilla, lassi and fresh juices found many takers, while those observing fasts enjoyed makhana and peanuts. Groups gathered around food counters before returning to the dance floor for another round of Garba.“I came here for Garba, but the food and activity stalls made it a complete evening out. We kept moving between the dance floor, food stalls and craft counters,” said Aditya Verma, an IT professional.As the evening gathered pace, DJ MaskBox, of international fame, arrived on stage with his characteristic aura of mystery, wearing a helmet that flashed only his initials. From hidden Gujarati gems to saucy flying saucers of the Udta Punjab kind, the DJ had curated a playlist that gave Lucknow a night to remember.Thoughtfully included were numbers like Saddi Gali and Main Nikla Gaddi Leke from films shot in Lucknow. From Dholi Taro to Shubha Mudgal’s throaty Mharo Dholna, there was hardly a number that wasn’t someone’s personal favourite.Dancers formed circles, matched their steps and moved in rhythm, with dandiya sticks clicking to the beat.The Skyhops dance group added to the spectacle with aerial lifts and a Ganesh Vandana performance, while Friendship Band brought another musical dimension to the celebrations.The evening also recognised participants who stood out. Pavika Tewari (5) won Best Kid Dancer, Madhurima (36) was named Best Dressed Lady, Prashant and Aneesha won Best Couple, while Mujtaba received the Best Dressed Man title.“The award was a bonus, but spending time together made it special,” said Aneesha, one half of the Best Couple winners.The reverential yet thundering Jai Ganesha Deva, sung by Shivam Mishra, got the early arrivals in step.A series of peppy filmi numbers, Gujarati folk tunes and other chartbusters had revellers showing off their best moves. articles.title: We can finally hear some of Wu-Tang Clan’s Once Upon A Time in Shaolin album
articles.summary: The podcast Pablo Torre Finds Out published two snippets of one-of-one Wu-Tang Clan’s Once Upon A Time in Shaolin as part of a new episode.
articles.body: Wu-Tang’s Once Upon A Time in Shaolin album has, for the most part, been extremely difficult to listen to, but you can now hear two snippets of the album thanks to the podcast Pablo Torre Finds Out, which just published an episode all about the exclusive record. Once Upon A Time in Shaolin has a long history, which Pablo Torre Finds Out goes into in detail. Disgraced pharmaceutical executive Martin Shkreli bought the only copy of the album, which cannot be commercially released until 2103, in 2015 at auction. Shkreli had to forfeit the album to the US government, and the government sold it in 2021 to the crypto art collective PleasrDAO, which has allowed it to be played at special exhibitions. Pablo Torre Finds Out, working with PleasrDAO, hosted a listening party for the album where they played it for Wu-Tang Clan member Method Man, who had never heard it up until that point. The podcast recorded the event and Method Man’s reaction, and you can hear two snippets from the album at 32:30 and 39:02 during the show. Method Man’s review? “I do not hate this album.”

articles.title: Judge tosses Timothy Busfield's indictment on child sex abuse charges
articles.summary: District Court Judge Joseph Montano granted Busfield's motion to throw out the grand jury indictment on Friday. Prosecutors can refile.
articles.body:
A New Mexico judge on Friday dismissed actor/director Timothy Busfield’s indictment on child sexual abuse charges.

District Court Judge Joseph Montano granted Busfield's motion to throw out the grand jury indictment.

"The State, however, remains free to institute new criminal proceedings against Defendant," the filing reads.

Busfield had been indicted on four counts of criminal sexual contact of a minor.
